掉转车马回到原路，趁迷路还不算太远。
打马在兰草水边行走，跑上椒木小山暂且停留。
既然进取不成反而获罪，就退回来重整当初的服饰。
裁剪碧绿荷叶做上衣，缝缀洁白荷花做下裳。
没人了解我也就罢了，只要我内心真正馥郁芳柔。
把帽子加得高高耸立，把佩带加得悠长飘逸。
芳香与光泽杂糅在一起，我光明纯洁的品质没有亏损。
忽然回过头来放眼远眺，打算去四面八方观览周游。
佩带缤纷繁多装饰华丽，馥郁香气散发得更加浓烈。
人生各有各的乐趣，我独爱好修洁习以为常。
姐姐女媭缠绵关切，反复告诫我说：鲧因刚直不顾性命，最终死在羽山荒野。
你为什么忠言直谏爱好修洁，独有你坚守这么多美好节操？
满屋都是普通花草，你却与众不同不肯佩带。
众人无法挨家挨户说明，谁会来体察我们的本心？
世人都互相吹捧成群结党，你为什么孤孤单单不听我的话？
依照前代圣贤道理节制性情，满腔忠愤至今不能平静。
渡过沅水湘水向南走去，我要向虞舜诉说衷情：夏启偷来九辩九歌，只顾放纵享乐。
不顾虑危难不考虑后果，五观因此发动了内乱。
后羿沉溺游猎玩乐，特别喜欢射杀大狐狸。
淫乱之徒本来没有好下场，寒浞杀了后羿霸占他的妻子。
寒浇自恃力气强大多么嚣张，放纵情欲不肯节制自己。
天天寻欢作乐忘乎所以，他的头颅因此掉落在地。
夏桀行为总违背常理，灾祸也就降临到他身上。
纣王把忠臣剁成肉酱，商朝国运因此不能长久。
商汤夏禹处事严肃恭敬，周初讲求正道没有差错。
举拔贤才任用能人，遵守规矩一点也不偏颇。
上天对一切公正无私，见有德之人就给予扶持帮助。
只有圣明德行高尚之人，才能享有天下的土地。
回顾前朝瞻望后代，观察人民衡量事情的标准。
哪有不义的事可以去干？
哪有不善的事可以去做？
即使面临死亡置身险境，回想当初志向我也毫不后悔。
不度量凿眼就削正榫头，前代贤人因此被剁成肉酱。
长声叹息泪流满面，哀伤我生不逢时如此不幸。
拿起柔软蕙草擦拭眼泪，热泪滚滚沾湿了我的衣襟。
铺开衣襟跪着慢慢陈述，我找到了正道心里明白。
驾着玉龙乘上凤车，风尘仆仆我将要上天远行。
清晨从苍梧山启程，傍晚就到达昆仑山上的悬圃。
想在灵琐稍作停留，太阳匆匆西沉暮色将至。
命令羲和慢些赶车，望见崦嵫山不要急于靠近。
前面的路漫长又遥远，我将要上天下地到处寻觅。
让马在咸池饮水，把马缰绳拴在扶桑树上。
折下若木枝条遮挡太阳，姑且在这里自由自在徜徉。
前面让月神望舒开路，后面让风神飞廉跟从奔忙。
鸾鸟凤凰在前面警戒，雷师却说还没有安排妥当。
命令凤凰展翅飞腾，要日日夜夜不停飞翔。
旋风聚集连结在一起，率领云霓前来迎接。
云霓越聚越多忽离忽合，五光十色上下飘浮荡漾。
叫天帝守门人把门打开，他却倚着天门冷冷把我观望。
日光渐暗天色将晚，我编结着幽兰久久伫立。
世道混乱污浊不分贤愚，喜欢嫉妒别人的美德抹煞长处。
清晨我将要渡过白水河，登上阆风山把马拴住。
忽然回头眺望涕泪涟涟，哀叹高丘上竟然没有神女。
匆匆来到春神青帝宫，折下琼枝系在佩带上。
趁着鲜花还没有凋落，去寻找下界可以接受馈赠的美人。
命令云神丰隆驾起云彩，去寻找宓妃居住的地方。
解下佩带束好书信，请蹇修前去为我做媒。
云霓纷纷簇集聚散离合，宓妃态度乖戾难以说合。
晚上宓妃回到穷石过夜，清晨她在洧盘水边洗发梳妆。
宓妃自恃美貌骄傲自大，整天寻欢作乐恣意游荡。
她虽然美丽却十分无礼，我放弃她改做别的追求。
览观四面八方遥远之地，周游天空之后我降临下界。
望见高耸巍峨的瑶台，看见有娀氏的美女简狄。
请鸩鸟前去为我做媒，鸩鸟却告诉我说简狄不好。
雄鸠叫唤着飞去说媒，我又嫌它太轻佻花言巧语。
心中犹豫迟疑不决，想自己去又觉得不合礼义。
凤凰已接受了聘礼，恐怕高辛氏已经抢先迎娶。
想到远方去又无处安居，只好四处游荡流浪逍遥。
趁着少康还没有成家，有虞氏还留着两位姚姓姑娘。
媒人笨拙口才又差，恐怕说合不能稳固牢靠。
世道浑浊嫉妒贤能，喜好遮蔽美德宣扬恶行。
闺中美人如此难以接近，贤明君王又始终不肯醒悟。
怀着一腔衷情无处抒发，我怎么能忍受这样到老！
找来灵草和细竹片，请灵氛为我占卜吉凶。
灵氛说：双方都美好必定能结合，但谁真正修洁值得爱慕？
想想天下这么广阔远大，难道只有这里才有美女吗？
努力远游不要疑惑，哪个寻求美女的人会放过你？
世间哪里没有芳草，为什么苦苦眷恋故园？
世道黑暗使人眼光迷乱，谁能辨别我们的善恶？
人们好恶本来就不相同，只是这帮小人特别古怪。
把艾草挂满腰间，反而说幽兰不可佩带。
连草木美恶都辨别不清，对美玉怎么能做出正确评价？
取来粪土塞满自己的香囊，反而说申椒一点也不芬芳。
想听从灵氛吉祥的占卜，心里却犹豫迟疑不决。
听说巫咸将在傍晚降神，我带着花椒香米前去迎候。
百神遮天蔽日一齐降临，九嶷山众神纷纷前去迎接。
巫咸灵光四射显示神异，告诉我往日君臣遇合的故事。
应该努力上天下地寻求，去寻找意气相投的同道知己。
商汤夏禹严谨求访贤臣，伊尹皋陶就能与他们协调和合。
只要内心真正爱好修洁，何必一定要靠媒人撮合说合？
傅说在傅岩筑墙劳作，武丁重用他毫不怀疑。
吕望曾经做过屠夫，遇到周文王就被举用为太师。
宁戚喂牛时敲牛角唱歌，齐桓公听了请他辅佐国政。
趁着年岁还没有衰老，时机也还没有完全丧失殆尽。
只怕杜鹃鸟叫得太早，使得百草都失去芬芳香气。
为什么我的玉佩这么高贵美丽，人们却要把它遮蔽埋藏？
这帮小人不讲信用，恐怕出于嫉妒要把它折断毁伤。
时世纷乱变化无常，我怎么能在这里长久停留？
兰草和芷草失去了芬芳，荃草和蕙草变成了茅草。
为什么往日的这些香草，今天都变成了荒野的蒿艾？
难道还有别的缘故吗？这是不好修洁造成的祸害。
原以为兰草可以依靠，谁知它华而不实虚有其表。
抛弃美德追随世俗，勉强列入众芳实在让人羞愧。
椒草专横谄媚傲慢自大，榝草又想充入香囊冒充芬芳。
它们拼命钻营追求权位，又怎么能敬重芬芳美德？
本来世俗风气就是随波逐流，又有谁能不发生变化？
看到椒兰尚且变成这样，何况揭车江离这些普通芳草？
只有我的玉佩最可贵，它的美质被人抛弃一直到今。
浓郁的香气难以消散，芬芳至今还没有完全消褪。
保持香气和欢愉自得其乐，姑且飘游四方寻求美女。
趁着玉佩还鲜丽华美，我要上天下地四处观览寻访。
灵氛已告诉我吉祥的占辞，选个吉日我将要启程远行。
折下玉树枝条作为珍馐，精磨玉屑作为旅途的干粮。
为我驾起飞龙，用美玉和象牙装饰我的车乘。
心志不同怎么能共处？
我将远走高飞自动疏远他们。
把行程转向昆仑山下，路途遥远继续周游观览。
云霞虹霓飞扬遮住阳光，车上玉铃叮当作响声震云天。
清晨从天河渡口出发，傍晚就到达了西方的尽头。
凤凰展开翅膀承托旌旗，高高飞翔整齐庄严。
忽然走到了流沙地带，沿着赤水道路从容徘徊。
指挥蛟龙在渡口架设桥梁，招呼西皇渡我过河去。
路途遥远又充满艰险，传令众车在路旁等待。
经过不周山向左转去，目标直指西海作为约会之地。
聚集了千辆战车，玉制车轮并排齐驱向前。
驾车的八龙蜿蜒前进，车上云旗随风舒卷飘扬。
定下心来慢慢前行，神思驰骋飞向遥远云天。
演奏《九歌》跳起《韶》舞，姑且借此时光寻找欢乐。
升起皇祖的灵光普照，忽然看到了我的故乡。
仆从悲伤马也怀恋，退缩回头不肯走向前方。
尾声：算了吧！
国内既然没有人了解我，又何必苦苦思念故国故都！
既然没有人能和我共行美政，我将追随彭咸到他居住的地方！
en_lines: A prince of high ancient lineage am I; my noble father bore the name Bo Yong.
When Saturn stood in Meng Zou, the first month, on the day Geng Yin I was born.
My father weighed my natal horoscope with care, and bestowed on me a name most fair: he called me True Form, upright and just, and gave me Ling Jun as my style.
Richly endowed with inward grace am I, and add to it my cultivated art.
I wear river sage and angelica sweet, and twine autumn orchids as my girdle meet.
Time flows like rushing water I cannot o'ertake; I fear the years will not for my sake wait.
At dawn I pluck magnolia on the highland slope, at eve I pick winter herbs on the islet's hope.
The sun and moon speed onward without stay; spring and autumn alternate on their way.
Seeing the trees and plants shed leaves and die, I fear my Fair One too will fade and sigh.
Why not cast off your faults in manhood's prime? Why not change the course of this old time?
Mount the swift steed and gallop far and wide! Come, I will lead the way and be your guide.
The three ancient kings were pure and perfectly bright; all fragrant flowers gathered in their sight.
Pepper and cassia mingled in their train; not only orchids wove their fragrant chain.
How noble Yao and Shun, straight in their way; they followed the right path and found the day.
How reckless Jie and Zhou in their mad pride; they took dark paths and stumbled far and wide.
The partisans seek pleasure, base and vain; their road is dark, narrow, and full of pain.
Do I fear disaster shall befall my own life? I fear the royal chariot will crash in strife.
I hasten running before and after thee, to follow where the former kings did be.
My sovereign reads not my true heart within; he heeds slander and rages in chagrin.
I know full well plain speech brings woe in train; I bear it, yet I cannot it restrain.
I point to ninefold Heaven as my witness true: all is for my Sacred One, for you.
We swore to meet at the hour of dusk, they say, but halfway you turned and changed your way.
At first you made a covenant firm with me, then you repented and turned to other see.
It is not hard to bid you now farewell; I grieve your changing mind, infidel.
I planted nine acres of orchids fine, and sowed a hundred mu of fragrant vine.
I laid out plots of sweet herbs row on row, mixed licorice and angelica to grow.
I hoped their leaves would grow luxuriant and tall, that I might reap them when due time did call.
What though they wither, fade and fall around? I grieve the fragrant weeds defile the ground.
Men throng to power with greedy, grasping eyes; their avarice never knows when to rise.
They judge all others by their own base heart, and shoot their envious darts on every part.
They rush in chase of gain and worldly fleet, things which my heart holds not precious or sweet.
Old age draws near, creeping on step by step; I fear my fair name may not make its repute.
At dawn I drink dew dropped from magnolia flowers; at eve I eat the fallen chrysanthemum bowers.
If but my heart be true, steadfast and fair, what matter if I waste with haggard care?
I dig up magnolia roots to tie white herbs, and string the figwort's falling blooms in curbs.
I bend cassia twigs to bind orchids sweet, twist ivy ropes long, neat and meet.
I follow where the ancient worthies trod, not in the garb of the base vulgar crowd.
Though I suit not the men of this vile age, I'll keep Peng Xian's heritage on my stage.
I heave long sighs and wipe my flowing tears, lamenting life's hard road through all the years.
Though I love beauty and my passions tie, at morn I'm scolded, and at eve cast by.
They blame me for my orchid girdle fair, and chide me for the angelica I wear.
But these are things my heart holds truly dear; I'd die a thousand deaths nor feel regret nor fear.
I blame my Sacred One, so reckless, wild, who never deigns to read a true man's heart beguiled.
The women envy me my moth-eyebrows fine; they slander me, saying I love base design.
The vulgar crowd loves cunning tricks and lies; they turn from rules and change their old device.
They leave the straight line to pursue crooked ways; they compete in base compliance all their days.
Sad and despondent, lost in bitter woe, alone I suffer in this age so low.
I'd rather die a sudden death and drift away than bear the base hypocrite's vile play.
The eagle soars alone, not with the common flock; so has it been since ancient times, from rock.
How can the square be fitted to the round? How can strange paths on common ground be found?
I bend my heart, subdue my will's command; bear reproach and bear shame's heavy hand.
To die for truth, keep pure and white, unspotted, was ever prized by ancient sages, unforgotten.
I rue I failed to see my way before; long I stand waiting, then turn back once more.
I turn my chariot to the old road again, before I stray too far in error's lane.
I walk my horse where orchids fringe the shore, then gallop to pepper hill to rest once more.
Advancing brought but reproach and bitter pain; I will retire and mend my first dress again.
I make a coat of lotus leaves so green, and gather hibiscus for a robe between.
If none knows me, let it be as it may, if but my heart be truly sweet and gay.
I make my cap rise high and higher still; my lengthened pendants sway with noble will.
Though fragrance mingle with the filth and mire, my radiant honour suffers no impair.
I turn my head and let my gaze run free, to see the four far corners of the sea.
My girdle ornaments are rich and rare; their fragrance spreads and fills the very air.
Each man has his own joy in life to hold; I love my beauty as my way grows old.
Though I be torn limb from limb, I'll not change; how could my heart be cowed by punishment strange?
My sister Xu, with tender, anxious sigh, chides me again and again with tearful eye: Gun was too straight and lost his life thereby, and perished at last on Mount Yu's bare lie.
Why must you speak so plain, love beauty so, alone holding these rare virtues that grow?
They fill their rooms with common weeds and tare, yet you stand apart and none of these will wear.
You cannot explain to every house, each door; who then will understand our inmost core?
Men form cliques and love friends, base and blind; why stand alone and will not hear my mind?
I follow ancient sages' rule of right, sighing my full heart bears this bitter plight.
I cross Yuan and Xiang, southward I go, to lay my plaint before King Shun, I trow: Qi stole the Nine Songs and Nine Debates, and Kang gave himself to self-indulgent fates.
He recked not danger, nor looked long ahead; his five sons brought rebellion to his bed.
Yi gave himself to hunting and base pleasure, and loved to shoot great foxes at his leisure.
But wanton men rarely come to good end; Zhuo killed him and took his wife as friend.
Ao relied upon his mighty strength, indulged his lusts and checked himself at length.
Daily he revelled, thought not of his fate, until his own head fell from its high estate.
King Jie of Xia defied all right and rule, and so in due time met disaster's pool.
Zhou of Yin hewed his ministers to meat; the Yin dynasty fell, its reign complete.
Tang and Yu were reverent, grave and wise; the Zhou kings ruled right beneath the skies.
They raised the worthy and employed the able, kept to the law, from bias stable.
High Heaven is impartial in its way; it sees men's virtue and lends them its ray.
None but the wise, the virtuous and great may rule the earth below and hold its state.
I look before and after, far and wide, observe the rules by which all men abide.
What man without right can ever gain his end?
What man without good can ever heaven bend?
I stand where death and danger meet my eye; looking back I have no regret, no sigh.
Not measuring the hole they shaped the peg, the ancients were cut down, limb from limb, leg.
Again and again I sigh, sad at heart, lamenting I was born in evil part.
I take soft orchids to wipe rising tears that flood my robe and wet my lapel gears.
Kneeling upon my outspread robe I speak my mind; I have found the middle path, true and kind.
I ride jade dragons, phoenixes before, and on the rushing dust wind I soar.
At dawn I set out from Cangwu's height; at eve I reach the Hanging Garden's light.
I wish to linger at this spirit gate, but the sun hurries on, it grows late.
I bid Xihe to slow her chariot's career; look towards Yanzi, draw not yet near.
The way ahead is long and far-reaching; I'll search high and low for my ideal, seeking.
I water my horses at Xianchi's brink, tie my reins to Fusang tree, I think.
I break a Ruo branch to brush back the sun, and wander freely there till day is done.
Before me Wangshu rides to clear the way; behind me Feilian follows without delay.
The phoenix goes before to warn and guide; the Thunder Lord says all is not yet plied.
I bid the phoenix rise on soaring wing, continue day and night without resting.
The whirlwinds gather, dense and dark, and lead cloud banners to meet me, mark.
The clouds swirl, part, gather, part again; bright hues dance above, below, they reign.
I bid heaven's gatekeeper open wide, but he leans on the gate and turns aside.
The light grows dim, the day draws to its end; twining orchids I stand, waiting, lonely friend.
The world is foul, confused, knows not the true; they hide men's worth, view all with envy due.
At dawn I will cross White Water's flowing stream, climb Langfeng Hill and tie my horse, I deem.
Suddenly I look back, my tears fall fast; grieved that on this high hill no fair goddess passed.
I hurry to the Spring God's palace fair, break a jade bough to lengthen my girdle there.
Before the jade blossoms fade and fall, seek a fair maiden below to give them all.
I bid Fenglong ride upon the cloud to find where Fu Fei's dwelling may be proud.
I loose my girdle cord to pledge my word, send Jian Xiu as messenger to her, my lord.
The clouds swirl round, drift apart again; she grows perverse, her heart is hard to gain.
At night she returns to Qiongshi to dwell; at dawn she washes her hair at Weipan well.
She prides herself on beauty, arrogant, daily wandering in self-indulgent want.
Though truly fair she lacks all courtesy; I will leave her, seek other where I may be.
I gaze across the earth's four farthest ends; after circling heaven, to earth I descend.
I see the lofty tower of Yao stand tall, and find fair Jiandi dwelling there withal.
I bid the poison bird go make my suit; it tells me she is not fair, not good to boot.
The turtledove flies off with merry cry; I hate its lightness and its treachery.
My heart is hesitating, full of doubt; to go myself would not be right, no rout.
The phoenix has already borne my gifts; I fear Gao Xin will be before me, swift.
I would fly far but find no resting place; I wander idly for a little space.
Before Shao Kang has wedded, there's still chance; the two fair Yao ladies wait in Yu's stance.
My messengers weak, my matchmakers poor, I fear their words will not be strong and sure.
The world is foul, envies the worthy man, loves hiding virtue, praising evil plan.
The inner chamber is so deep, so far; the wise king wakes not, knows not who we are.
I bear my passion, cannot it impart; how can I bear this forever in my heart?
I take magic herbs and bamboo divining sticks, bid witch Ling Fen divine my fate and tricks.
He said: Two beauties surely must unite; who is truly fair will not love's delight?
Think how wide and broad the nine domains; is it only here that beauty reigns?
Go far away, he said, doubt not, delay; who seeks fair beauty will not turn you away?
What place is there without sweet fragrant grass? Why cling so fondly to your old home, alas?
The world is dark, dazzles the gazing eye; who can tell my evil from my high?
Men's likes and dislikes differ, well we know; but these base partisans are strange to show.
They wear foul mugwort hanging from their waist, and say sweet orchid is not fit to taste.
They cannot tell fair plants from weeds aright; how can they judge a precious gem's true light?
They fill their sachets full of stinking dung, and say the pepper has no fragrance, young.
I wished to follow Ling Fen's lucky guess, yet in my heart I doubt, in deep distress.
Witch Wu Xian will descend at eventide; I carry pepper and rice to greet his guide.
The hundred gods come down in shadowy train; the spirits of Jiuyi come to meet them amain.
Their glorious spirits flash with brilliant light, and tell me of auspicious fate so bright.
He said: Rise high and low, search far and wide, seek those whose standards match your own true pride.
Tang and Yu reverently sought their fit mate; Yi and Gao Yao helped them rule the state.
If but your heart loves beauty and true grace, what need have you of matchmaker's base place?
Yue laboured with his hammer at Fu Yan; Wu Ding used him, no doubt in his plan.
Lü Wang was once a butcher, knife in hand; he met King Wen and gained high command.
Ning Qi sang as he fed his ox at night; Duke Huan of Qi heard him and made him knight.
Before your years have all drawn to their close, while time has not yet reached its final throes.
Fear lest the cuckoo sings before its time, making all hundred herbs lose fragrance prime.
How fair and tall my jade pendant doth stand! The crowd would darken it on every hand.
These partisans are faithless, false in word; I fear their envy will break it, absurd.
The age is confused, changes every day; how can I linger here, long stay?
Orchid and iris have lost all their sweet; the sweet herbs have turned into common wheat.
Why are the fragrant plants of days gone by turned now to stinking weeds that fade and die?
What other reason can there be for this? The harm of not cultivating beauty, miss!
I thought the orchid could be trusted well; it proved mere show, no substance in its shell.
It cast its beauty off to follow fashion, falsely listed among the fragrant passion.
The pepper is cunning, arrogant and vain; even dogwood would fill the perfume chain.
Since they all press to advance and climb high, what fragrance can they ever magnify?
The vulgar flow with every changing tide; who then can keep unchanged his true heart's pride?
Seeing pepper and orchid fall so low, what of the lesser herbs, shall they not go?
Only my pendant is worth treasuring; its beauty spurned, it passes through everything.
Its fragrance is full, it cannot fade; its scent lingers still, does not degrade.
I adjust my pendants, walk in measured pleasure, and wander far to seek my beauty's treasure.
While my adornments are in their full prime, I will look high and low, travel and climb.
Since Ling Fen gave me his auspicious word, I choose a lucky day to leave, my lord.
I break jade branches for my dainty food, grind jade fragments to make my travel good.
For me they yoke the flying dragons bright; my chariot is wrought of jade and ivory white.
How can two differing hearts e'er find accord?
I will go far away, of my own accord.
I turn my course towards Kunlun's mountain height; the way is long as I roam in my flight.
I raise cloud banners darkening the sky; my jade bells chime their tinkling melody.
At dawn I leave the Ford of Heavenly Sky; at eve I reach the world's western end nigh.
The phoenix spreads its wings to bear my flags, soaring high on steady wing, no drags.
Suddenly I pass the Flowing Sands of fire, and follow the Red Water, wandering nigher.
I bid the dragons bridge the ford for me, call the West Sovereign to carry me over the sea.
The road is long and hard, full of strife; I bid my carriages wait by the path for life.
I pass Buzhou Mountain, turn left at last; point to the Western Sea as our meeting past.
I gather a thousand chariots in train; line up their jade wheels, race on amain.
Eight dragons draw my chariot, winding on; cloud banners flutter in the wind, foregone.
I still my heart, slow down the pace again; my spirit soars to heights beyond men's ken.
I play the Nine Songs, dance the royal Shao dance, borrowing time to find a little chance.
I climb the glorious brightness of high heaven, when suddenly I gaze on my old home, leaven.
My driver grieves, my horses long for home; they curve back, look around, refuse to roam.
Envoi: It is done! It is ended!
In all the kingdom no man knows me true; why must I long for my old home so blue?
Since none will join me to rule with fair art, I'll go to join Peng Xian in his last abode!
en_text: Descendant of Gao Yang am I, my noble father Bo Yong by name.
When Jupiter stood in Meng Zou, on Geng Yin day I was born.
My father divined my birth, bestowed the name Zheng Ze, Ling Jun the courtesy name.
Endowed with inner grace, I diligently cultivated my virtue.
Clad in river moss and angelica, autumn orchids strung as my girdle.
Time rushes like a torrent I cannot o'ertake, the years wait for no man.
At dawn I gathered magnolia on hills, at eve picked evergreens on the isle.
Sun and moon hasten without delay, spring and autumn in endless turn.
Seeing plants wither from bloom to fall, I fear my own prime fading away.
Why not cast off corruption in your prime? Why not reform these ways?
Mount your steed and gallop ahead, I shall lead the way before you!
How pure were the three ancient kings, around them gathered all virtuous men.
Pepper and cinnamon grew in profusion, not only orchids strung as pendants.
Yao and Shun were bright and just, they followed the straight path to broad ways.
How reckless were Jie and Zhou, seeking crooked paths they met their ruin.
Partisans seek selfish pleasure, their road is dark with perils.
Do I fear disaster for myself? I fear the royal chariot will overturn!
I hurried forward and stayed back, tracing the footsteps of former kings.
The king perceived not my loyal heart, trusted slander and raged against me.
I knew frank words invited disaster, yet endured not, I had to speak.
I call high heaven to bear witness, all was done for my sovereign's sake.
We pledged to meet at twilight, yet he changed course halfway!
At first we made a solemn pledge, then he turned back to other plans.
I grieve not at parting from my lord, but sorrow at his fickle heart.
I planted nine acres of orchids, sowed a hundred acres of angelica.
Rows of liuyi and qieju grew, interspersed with duruo and fragrant zhi.
I hoped they would flourish tall, to reap them when their season came.
What matter if they wither? I grieve fragrant plants run wild and change.
Petty men scramble for power and wealth, their greed insatiable, endless.
Forgiving themselves yet suspecting others, scheming in mutual envy.
Chasing gain like galloping horses, these things my heart holds not urgent.
Old age creeps steadily upon me, I fear my name will not be established.
At dawn I drink magnolia dew, at eve eat chrysanthemum petals fresh.
If my heart remains steadfast and pure, what matter if I grow gaunt and worn?
I tie angelica to magnolia roots, string pistils of climbing figs.
I lift cinnamon twined with orchids, twist long ropes of hushang vine.
I follow attire of ancient sages, not vulgar garb of petty men today.
Though I match not this age's customs, I follow Peng Xian's virtuous example.
I heave long sighs and wipe tears, grieving the people's lives of hardship.
Though I loved virtue and restrained self, at dawn rebuked, at dusk exiled.
They assail me for orchid pendants, blame me for gathering angelica.
These things my heart truly loves, nine deaths would bring me no regret.
I resent the king's wild recklessness, he never understands my loyal heart.
Women envy my moth-eyebrow beauty, spread lies that I am wanton, base.
The world excels in cunning tricks, turns from right rules to change measures.
Turning from straight lines to crooked curves, competing in flattery as their rule.
Downcast, sorrowful and distressed, alone I bear such hardship now.
I'd rather die and vanish at once, than adopt vulgar sycophantic ways.
The eagle flocks not with common birds, this has been true since ancient times.
How can square and round fit together? How can different minds live in peace?
I bow my heart and repress my will, endure blame and bear humiliation.
Preserving purity, dying for the right, ancient sages truly valued this.
I regret seeing not my path clearly, hesitate and now will turn my chariot.
Turn my carriage to retrace my road, before I wander too far astray.
Walk my horse by the orchid stream, rest on the hill of pepper trees.
Since advancement brings condemnation, retire to mend my former attire.
Make a coat of green lotus leaves, sew a skirt of white lotus blossoms.
Let none understand me if they will, so long as my heart remains fragrant.
Raise my cap to tower high above, lengthen my pendants to sway with grace.
Fragrance and radiance mingle together, my pure bright spirit remains unblemished.
Suddenly turn my head to gaze afar, resolve to roam four corners of earth.
My pendants are rich in adornment, sweet fragrance spreads more widely still.
Each man has his own delights, I alone love virtue as my constant way.
E'en if my body be torn asunder, my heart can never be altered.
My sister Nü Xu, anxious and caring, warned me again and again: Gun was stubborn and perished for it, his body abandoned on Yu Mountain wild.
Why must you speak frankly and love virtue, upholding such purity alone?
Rooms are filled with common weeds, yet you stand apart and wear them not.
We cannot explain to every door, who will come examine our true hearts?
The world sides together in cliques, why stand alone and heed not my words?
Following ancient sages to moderate my nature, my heart burns with indignation still.
Crossing Yuan and Xiang southward, I lay my cause before Emperor Shun: Qi stole Nine Bian and Nine Songs, indulged in wanton self-pleasure.
Thinking not of danger nor consequence, his son Wu Guan raised rebellion.
Hou Yi abandoned himself to hunting, fond of shooting the great foxes.
The reckless come to no good end, Han Zhuo slew him and took his wife.
Han Ao relied on o'erwhelming might, indulging passions without restraint.
Day after day he reveled forgetting self, until his head was severed from his neck.
Jie of Xia acted against all reason, calamity came down upon him.
Zhou of Shang minced his loyal ministers, Shang dynasty could not endure.
Tang and Yu were reverent and solemn, early Zhou followed the Way without error.
They raised the worthy and employed the able, observing rules without partiality.
High Heaven is impartial in all things, sees virtue and lends its support.
Only sages of true noble virtue, may possess the lands beneath the sky.
I look back through hist'ry and forward, observe standards by which men judge things.
What unjust deed can ever be done?
What evil act can ever be practiced?
E'en facing death and mortal peril, looking back I feel no regret at all.
Shaping tenon without measuring socket, ancient sages were cruelly slain for this.
I heave long sighs and my tears stream, saddened I was born in ill-fated time.
Taking soft orchids to wipe my eyes, hot tears flow down and soak my garment.
I spread robes and kneel to state my case, having found the right way, my heart is clear.
Yoked to jade dragons, phoenix chariot borne, in whirlwind I ascend to journey heav'nward.
At dawn I depart from Cangwu Mountain, at eve reach Xuanpu on Mount Kunlun.
I wish to linger at the spirit gate, but sun hastens west and dusk falls fast.
I bid Xi He slow her chariot pace, not rush toward Mount Yanzi as she nears.
The road before me is long and far, I'll search high and low for my heart's desire.
Water my dragons at Xianchi Pool, tie my reins on Fusang mulberry tree.
Break a Ruo branch to shade the sun, wander there freely for a little while.
Ahead moon goddess Wang Shu leads the way, behind wind god Fei Lian follows fast.
Luan birds and phoenixes clear the path, but Thunder Lord says all is not ready.
I command phoenixes to soar on wings, flying onward day and night without cease.
Whirlwinds gather and swirl around me, leading clouds and rainbows to welcome me.
Clouds and rainbows cluster, part, reunite, myriad colors shifting, rising, falling.
I bid heav'n's gatekeeper open his gate, but he leans 'gainst the door and stares coldly.
Light fades and evening darkens sky, I plait orchid garlands and wait long.
The world is foul, knows not worth from waste, loves to envy virtue, t'obscure excellence.
At dawn I'll cross the White Water River, climb Langfeng Peak and tether my horses.
Looking back suddenly my tears flow free, lamenting that on high hill there's no goddess.
I hasten to the palace of the Green Emperor, break a jade branch to lengthen my pendant.
Before blossoms fade and fall, seek a maiden below to receive my gift.
I command Feng Long to ride the clouds, to seek where goddess Fu Fei makes her home.
Loosening my girdle to send as pledge, I ask Jian Xiu to act as my matchmaker.
Clouds gather and swirl in profusion, but Fu Fei is perverse and hard to persuade.
At night she returns to Qiongshi to rest, at dawn washes hair at Weipan stream.
Proud of her beauty, arrogant, she revels day after day in wanton pleasure.
Though beautiful she lacks propriety, I abandon her and seek elsewhere.
I gaze across four corners of vast earth, descend after roaming across the heavens.
Behold the lofty Terrace of Jasper, I see Jian Di, fair maid of Yousong clan.
I bid the pois'nous dove to be my envoy, it tells me Jian Di is not good and true.
The male turtledove flies to matchmake, I find him too frivolous, full of false words.
My heart hesitates in indecision, wishing to go myself yet deeming it wrong.
The phoenix has already taken betrothal gifts, I fear Gao Xin has preceded me in winning her.
Thinking of wand'ring far but finding no rest, I wander idly roaming here and there.
Before Shao Kang has taken him a wife, there remain two princesses of the Yu clan.
My envoy is feeble and my words are clumsy, I fear the match will not be secured.
The age is foul and envies worthy men, delighting to obscure virtue and exalt vice.
Beauties in chambers are unreachable, the wise king never wakens t'understanding.
I hold loyal heart with no outlet, how can I endure thus until life's end?
I take sacred herbs and bamboo slips, ask Ling Fen to divine my fortune.
He says: Two beauties must surely unite, but who is truly pure and worthy of love?
Consider how vast the world is, can beauteous women exist only in this land?
Go forth and doubt not, who seeks beauty would ever pass you by?
Where are there no fragrant plants? Why cling so stubbornly to your old home?
The world is dark and men's eyes are blinded, who can discern our good and evil?
Men's likes and dislikes differ, these men are stranger than all others!
They wear stinking mugwort at their waists, say delicate orchids are unfit to wear.
They cannot tell plants from one another, how can they judge precious jade correctly?
They fill their sachets with dung and filth, say Sichuan pepper has no true fragrance.
I wish to follow Ling Fen's auspice, yet my heart hesitates full of doubt.
I hear Wu Xian will descend at dusk, I carry pepper and rice to meet him.
The hundred gods descend in radiant procession, spirits of Jiu Yi come thronging t'welcome.
Wu Xian glows with numinous brightness, tells me tales of meetings of lord and minister.
He says: Strive to search high and low, seek one whose principles accord with yours.
Tang and Yu earnestly sought worthy ministers, Yi Yin and Gao Yao joined them in harmony.
If your heart truly loves cultivation, what need for matchmakers and go-betweens?
Fu Yue labored building walls at Fu Yan, Wu Ding employed him without slightest doubt.
Lü Wang was once a butcher in the market, King Wen found him and made him Preceptor.
Ning Qi sang while feeding oxen, Duke Huan heard him and took him as minister.
Act before your years have fully aged, before your appointed time has run out.
Fear lest the cuckoo cry too early, making all hundred herbs lose their fragrance.
Why is my jade pendant so surpassing fair, that men should obscure and hide it away?
These men are faithless and full of falsehood, fearing envy they will break and destroy it.
The times are chaos, shifting, changing, how can I linger here for long?
Orchids and angelica have lost fragrance, pollia and pollia turned to common reeds.
Why have these fragrant plants of old, turned today to worthless weeds of the field?
Is there any other reason? 'Tis harm wrought by failing to cultivate virtue!
I once thought the orchid was reliable, but it proves false, empty of substance.
Abandoning virtue to follow the crowd, 'tis shaming to see it 'mong the fragrant.
Pepper grows cunning, flatt'ring, arrogant, thornbush strives to fill the sachet.
They press and push to gain advancement, how can they value true fragrance?
Such is the vulgar way, drifting with current, who can remain unchanging in this world?
Seeing pepper and orchid change thus, how much more the lesser common plants?
Only my jade pendant remains truly precious, its beauty rejected by all until this day.
Its rich fragrance cannot be dispelled, its scent lingers still, undiminished.
I maintain harmony and find pleasure, wand'ring forth to seek the beauty I desire.
While my pendant is still bright, resplendent, I'll range high and low to search the world.
Ling Fen has given auspicious divination, I choose a lucky day to start my journey.
I break jade tree branches for my food, grind fine jade dust as provisions for the road.
Flying dragons are harnessed to my chariot, adorned with ivory and jade in fine array.
How can hearts at odds dwell together?
I will go far away, estranged from them all.
I turn my course toward Kunlun Mountains, the road is long as I wander and observe.
Clouds and rainbows rise t'obscure the sun, jade bells ring with clear celestial sound.
At dawn I depart from Ford of Heaven, at evening reach the uttermost western end.
Phoenixes spread wings bearing banners, flying on high in solemn stately flight.
Suddenly I find myself in shifting sands, following Red River I wander slowly on.
I bid dragons form a bridge across the ford, summon Western Sov'reign to ferry me across.
The road is long and fraught with perils, I command retinues to wait by the road.
Passing Mount Buzhou I turn to the left, making Western Sea my appointed goal.
I gather a thousand chariots around me, jade wheels aligned to race forward together.
Eight dragons draw my chariot winding on, cloud banners flutter and stream in the wind.
I calm my spirit and slow my pace, thoughts soar aloft to the distant clouds.
I perform Nine Songs and dance Shao Dance, seizing this moment to find fleeting joy.
As my ancestors' radiance rises bright, I suddenly catch sight of my old homeland.
My servants grieve and my horses long for home, they turn back heads and will not go forward.
Envoi: It is finished!
Since none within the kingdom knows me, why should I long for my native capital?
Since none will join me in righteous rule, I'll go to join Peng Xian in his dwelling place!
baihua_text:
我是上古帝王高阳氏的后裔，我伟大的先父名叫伯庸。
　　岁星在寅那年孟春正月庚寅之日，我降生到人间。
　　父亲观察我的生辰卦象，赐我美名正则，表字叫灵均。
　　我既有这么多内在美质，又不断加强自己的修养。
　　我披挂着江离和辟芷，把秋兰编织成佩带。
　　时光如急流飞逝我追赶不上，岁月不等人令我心慌。
　　早晨在山坡采集木兰，傍晚在小洲摘取宿莽。
　　时光迅速逝去不能久留，四季更相代谢变化有常。
　　想到草木已由盛到衰，恐怕自己也逐渐衰老。
　　何不趁壮年抛弃污秽？为什么不改变这种法度？
　　乘上骏马纵横驰骋吧，我来在前面为你带路！
　　从前三王德行纯粹完美，众贤臣都聚集在他们周围。
　　那里杂生申椒和菌桂，哪里只有蕙草香芷连佩带！
　　唐尧虞舜多么光明正大，沿着正道登上坦途。
　　夏桀殷纣多么狂妄邪恶，贪图捷径最终走投无路。
　　结党营私之人苟且享乐，前途黑暗而充满险阻。
　　难道我害怕自身招祸？只担心国家为此倾覆！
　　我前前后后奔走照料，希望追上前王的足迹。
　　君王不体察我一片赤诚，反而听信谗言对我发怒。
　　我本知忠言直谏会招祸患，想忍耐却还是止不住要说。
　　我指着苍天作证，这一切都是为了君王的缘故。
　　当初约定黄昏为期，谁知道中途改了路！
　　当初既已与我约定，后来又反悔另有打算。
　　我并不难于与君王别离，只伤心他态度反复无常。
　　我栽培了九畹春兰，又种植了百亩秋蕙。
　　分垄栽培留夷和揭车，套种了杜衡与芳芷。
　　希望它们枝繁叶茂高大，等成熟时节我就收割。
　　枯萎凋零又有何妨，最痛心众芳草荒芜变质。
　　小人们争权夺利贪得无厌，搜刮财物永远没有满足。
　　他们宽恕自己猜忌别人，勾心斗角互相嫉妒。
　　像奔马追逐私利，这不是我心中所急。
　　衰老渐渐向我逼近，担心美名不能树立。
　　早晨饮木兰坠落的露水，晚上嚼秋菊初开的花瓣。
　　只要我情感坚贞品质美好，面黄肌瘦又有何妨。
　　用木兰根系上白芷，串起薜荔初开的花蕊。
　　举起菌桂联结蕙草，把胡绳搓得修长美丽。
　　我效法前贤装束，不与世俗小人相同。
　　虽不合今人习惯，愿依照彭咸留下的榜样。
　　长长叹息掩面流泪，哀伤人民生活多灾多难。
　　我虽爱好修洁严于律己，早晨进谏晚上就被罢官。
　　他们攻击我佩带蕙草，又指责我采集芳芷。
　　这是我心中追求的东西，就算多次死亡也不后悔。
　　怨愤君王荒唐放纵，始终不能体察我的忠心。
　　众女嫉妒我的蛾眉，造谣说我善于淫邪。
　　世俗本就善于投机取巧，违背规矩随意改变措施。
　　违背准绳追求邪曲，争着把苟合取容当作法度。
　　我烦闷忧愁失意不安，此时只有我独自遭受困厄。
　　宁可马上死去魂魄离散，也绝不做媚俗取巧的姿态。
　　雄鹰不与凡鸟同群，从古以来就是如此。
　　方与圆怎么能相合？志向不同怎么能相安？
　　委屈自己的心志，压抑自己的情感。
　　保持清白死于直道，本就是前代圣贤所推崇。
　　后悔当初没看清道路，迟疑一阵我要回头。
　　掉转车马回到原路，趁迷路还不算太远。
　　打马在兰草水边行走，跑上椒木小山暂作停留。
　　既然进取不成反而获罪，就退回来重整当初的服饰。
　　裁剪碧绿荷叶做上衣，缝缀洁白荷花做下裳。
　　没人了解我也就罢了，只要我内心真正芬芳。
　　把帽子加得高高耸立，把佩带加得悠长飘逸。
　　芳香与光泽杂糅在一起，我光明纯洁的品质没有亏损。
　　忽然回头放眼远眺，打算去四面八方观览周游。
　　佩带缤纷装饰华丽，馥郁香气散发得更加浓烈。
　　人生各有各的乐趣，我独爱好修洁习以为常。
　　就算被肢解我也不改变，志向岂能因受挫而改变？
　　姐姐女嬃缠绵关切，她反复告诫我说：鲧因刚直不顾性命，最终死在羽山荒野。
　　你为什么忠言直谏爱好修洁，独有这么多美好节操？
　　满屋都是普通花草，你却与众不同不肯佩带。
　　众人无法挨家挨户说明，谁会来体察我们的本心？
　　世人互相吹捧成群结党，为什么你孤孤单单不听我劝？
　　依前代圣贤节制性情，满腔忠愤至今不能平静。
　　渡过沅湘向南走，向虞舜诉说衷情：夏启偷来九辩九歌，只顾放纵享乐。
　　不顾危难不考虑后果，五观因此发动内乱。
　　后羿沉溺游猎玩乐，特别喜欢射杀大狐狸。
　　淫乱之徒本来没好下场，寒浞杀了他霸占他妻子。
　　寒浇自恃强大多么嚣张，放纵情欲不肯节制自己。
　　天天寻欢作乐忘乎所以，他的头颅因此掉落在地。
　　夏桀行为总违背常理，灾祸也就降临到他身上。
　　纣王把忠臣剁成肉酱，商朝国运因此不能长久。
　　商汤夏禹严肃恭敬，周初讲求正道没有差错。
　　举拔贤才任用能人，遵守规矩一点也不偏颇。
　　上天对一切公正无私，见有德之人就给予扶持。
　　只有圣明德行高尚之人，才能享有天下的土地。
　　回顾前朝瞻望后代，观察人民衡量事情的标准。
　　哪有不义之事可以去做？
　　哪有不善之事可以去做？
　　即使面临死亡险境，回想当初志向也毫不后悔。
　　不度量凿眼就削正榫头，前代贤人因此被剁成肉酱。
　　长声叹息泪流满面，哀伤我生不逢时如此不幸。
　　拿起柔软蕙草擦拭眼泪，热泪滚滚沾湿了我的衣襟。
　　铺开衣襟跪着慢慢陈述，我找到正道心里明白。
　　驾玉龙乘凤车，风尘仆仆我要上天远行。
　　清晨从苍梧山启程，傍晚到达昆仑悬圃。
　　想在灵琐稍作停留，太阳匆匆西沉暮色将至。
　　命令羲和慢些赶车，望见崦嵫山不要急于靠近。
　　前面的路漫长又遥远，我将上天下地到处寻觅。
　　让马在咸池饮水，把缰绳拴在扶桑树上。
　　折下若木枝条遮挡太阳，姑且在这里自在徜徉。
　　前面让月神望舒开路，后面让风神飞廉跟从奔忙。
　　鸾鸟凤凰在前面警戒，雷师却说还没安排妥当。
　　命令凤凰展翅飞腾，日日夜夜不停飞翔。
　　旋风聚集连结在一起，率领云霓前来迎接。
　　云霓越聚越多忽离忽合，五光十色上下飘浮荡漾。
　　叫天帝守门人开门，他却倚着天门冷冷观望。
　　日光渐暗天色将晚，我编结幽兰久久伫立。
　　世道混乱污浊不分贤愚，喜嫉妒美德抹煞长处。
　　清晨我将渡过白水河，登上阆风山把马拴住。
　　忽然回头眺望涕泪涟涟，哀叹高丘上竟然没有神女。
　　匆匆来到青帝春神宫，折下琼枝系在佩带上。
　　趁鲜花还没凋落，去寻找下界可馈赠的美人。
　　命令云神丰隆驾云，去寻找宓妃居住之处。
　　解下佩带束好书信，请蹇修前去为我做媒。
　　云霓纷纷簇集散离合，宓妃态度乖戾难以说合。
　　晚上宓妃回穷石过夜，清晨在洧盘水边洗发梳妆。
　　宓妃自恃美貌骄傲自大，整天寻欢作乐恣意游荡。
　　她虽美丽却十分无礼，我放弃她改做别的追求。
　　览观四面八方遥远之地，周游天空之后我降临下界。
　　望见巍峨高耸的瑶台，看到有娀氏美女简狄。
　　请鸩鸟前去为我做媒，鸩鸟却告诉我说简狄不好。
　　雄鸠叫唤飞去说媒，我又嫌它太轻佻花言巧语。
　　心中犹豫迟疑不决，想自己去又觉得不合礼义。
　　凤凰已接受了聘礼，恐怕高辛氏已抢先迎娶。
　　想远走高飞又无处安居，只好四处游荡流浪逍遥。
　　趁少康还没成家，有虞氏还留着两位姚姓姑娘。
　　媒人笨拙口才又差，恐怕说合不能稳固牢靠。
　　世道浑浊嫉妒贤能，喜好遮蔽美德宣扬恶行。
　　闺中美人如此难以接近，贤明君王又始终不肯醒悟。
　　怀着一腔衷情无处抒发，我怎么能忍受到老！
　　找来灵草和细竹片，请灵氛为我占卜吉凶。
　　灵氛说：两美必合，但谁真正修洁值得爱慕？
　　想想天下这么广阔远大，难道只有这里才有美女？
　　努力远游不要疑惑，哪个寻求美女的人会放过你？
　　世间哪里没有芳草，为什么苦苦眷恋故园？
　　世道黑暗使人眼光迷乱，谁能辨别我们的善恶？
　　人们好恶本就不同，这帮小人尤其古怪！
　　把艾草挂满腰间，反而说幽兰不可佩带。
　　连草木美恶都辨不清，对美玉怎能正确评价？
　　取来粪土塞满香囊，反而说申椒一点也不芬芳。
　　想听从灵氛吉祥占卜，心里却犹豫迟疑不决。
　　听说巫咸傍晚将神，带着花椒香米前去迎候。
　　百神遮天蔽日齐降临，九嶷山众神纷纷来迎接。
　　巫咸灵光四射显示神异，告诉我君臣遇合的故事。
　　他说：努力上天下地寻求，寻找意气相投的同道知己。
　　商汤夏禹严谨求访贤臣，伊尹皋陶与他们协调和合。
　　只要内心真正爱好修洁，何必一定要靠媒人撮合？
　　傅说在傅岩筑墙劳作，武丁重用他毫不怀疑。
　　吕望曾经做过屠夫，遇到周文王被举为太师。
　　宁戚喂牛时敲牛角唱歌，齐桓公听了请他辅政。
　　趁年岁还没衰老，时机也还没完全丧失。
　　只怕杜鹃鸟叫得太早，使得百草都失去芬芳香气。
　　为什么我玉佩这么高贵，人们却要把它遮蔽埋藏？
　　这帮小人不讲信用，恐怕因嫉妒要把它折断。
　　时世纷乱变化无常，我怎么能在这里长久停留？
　　兰草芷草失去芬芳，荃草蕙草变成了茅草。
　　为什么往日的这些香草，今天都变成了荒野的蒿艾？
　　难道还有别的缘故？这是不修美德造成的祸害！
　　原以为兰草可以依靠，谁知它华而不实虚有其表。
　　抛弃美德追随世俗，勉强列入众芳实在让人羞愧。
　　椒草专横谄媚傲慢自大，樧草又想充入香囊冒充芬芳。
　　拼命钻营追求权位，又怎么能敬重芬芳美德？
　　本就是世俗随波逐流，又有谁能不发生变化？
　　看到椒兰尚且变成这样，何况揭车江离这些普通芳草？
　　只有我玉佩最可贵，它的美质被人抛弃一直到今。
　　浓郁香气难以消散，芬芳至今还没完全消褪。
　　保持香气欢愉自得其乐，姑且飘游四方寻求美女。
　　趁我玉佩还鲜丽华美，我要上天下地四处寻访。
　　灵氛已告诉我吉祥占辞，选个吉日我将要启程远行。
　　折下玉树枝作为珍馐，精磨玉屑作为旅途干粮。
　　为我驾起飞龙，用美玉和象牙装饰我的车乘。
　　心志不同怎么能共处？
　　我将远走高飞自动疏远他们。
　　把行程转向昆仑山下，路途遥远继续周游观览。
　　云霞虹霓飞扬遮住阳光，车上玉铃叮当作响声震云天。
　　清晨从天河渡口出发，傍晚到达西方的尽头。
　　凤凰展开翅膀承托旌旗，高高飞翔整齐而庄严。
　　忽然走到了流沙地带，沿着赤水道路从容徘徊。
　　指挥蛟龙在渡口架设桥梁，招呼西皇渡我过河去。
　　路途遥远又充满艰险，传令众车在路旁等待。
　　经过不周山向左转去，目标直指西海作为约会之地。
　　聚集了千辆战车，玉制车轮并排齐驱向前。
　　八龙蜿蜒驾车前进，车上云旗随风舒卷飘扬。
　　定下心来慢慢前行，神思驰骋飞向遥远云天。
　　演奏《九歌》跳起《韶》舞，姑且借此时光寻找欢乐。
　　升起皇祖的灵光普照，忽然看到了我的故乡。
　　仆从悲伤马也怀恋，退缩回头不肯走向前方。
　　尾声：算了吧！
　　国内既然没人了解我，又何必苦苦思念故都！
　　既然没人能和我共行美政，我将追随彭咸到他居住的地方！
en_note: 《离骚》英译主体参考许渊冲《楚辞》英译本，部分散佚段落由诗藏本体论补译 (Shicang Translation)。
en_body: Descendant of Gao Yang am I, my noble father Bo Yong by name.
When Jupiter stood in Meng Zou, on Geng Yin day I was born.
My father divined my birth, bestowed the name Zheng Ze, Ling Jun the courtesy name.
Endowed with inner grace, I diligently cultivated my virtue.
Clad in river moss and angelica, autumn orchids strung as my girdle.
Time rushes like a torrent I cannot o'ertake, the years wait for no man.
At dawn I gathered magnolia on hills, at eve picked evergreens on the isle.
Sun and moon hasten without delay, spring and autumn in endless turn.
Seeing plants wither from bloom to fall, I fear my own prime fading away.
Why not cast off corruption in your prime? Why not reform these ways?
Mount your steed and gallop ahead, I shall lead the way before you!
How pure were the three ancient kings, around them gathered all virtuous men.
Pepper and cinnamon grew in profusion, not only orchids strung as pendants.
Yao and Shun were bright and just, they followed the straight path to broad ways.
How reckless were Jie and Zhou, seeking crooked paths they met their ruin.
Partisans seek selfish pleasure, their road is dark with perils.
Do I fear disaster for myself? I fear the royal chariot will overturn!
I hurried forward and stayed back, tracing the footsteps of former kings.
The king perceived not my loyal heart, trusted slander and raged against me.
I knew frank words invited disaster, yet endured not, I had to speak.
I call high heaven to bear witness, all was done for my sovereign's sake.
We pledged to meet at twilight, yet he changed course halfway!
At first we made a solemn pledge, then he turned back to other plans.
I grieve not at parting from my lord, but sorrow at his fickle heart.
I planted nine acres of orchids, sowed a hundred acres of angelica.
Rows of liuyi and qieju grew, interspersed with duruo and fragrant zhi.
I hoped they would flourish tall, to reap them when their season came.
What matter if they wither? I grieve fragrant plants run wild and change.
Petty men scramble for power and wealth, their greed insatiable, endless.
Forgiving themselves yet suspecting others, scheming in mutual envy.
Chasing gain like galloping horses, these things my heart holds not urgent.
Old age creeps steadily upon me, I fear my name will not be established.
At dawn I drink magnolia dew, at eve eat chrysanthemum petals fresh.
If my heart remains steadfast and pure, what matter if I grow gaunt and worn?
I tie angelica to magnolia roots, string pistils of climbing figs.
I lift cinnamon twined with orchids, twist long ropes of hushang vine.
I follow attire of ancient sages, not vulgar garb of petty men today.
Though I match not this age's customs, I follow Peng Xian's virtuous example.
I heave long sighs and wipe tears, grieving the people's lives of hardship.
Though I loved virtue and restrained self, at dawn rebuked, at dusk exiled.
They assail me for orchid pendants, blame me for gathering angelica.
These things my heart truly loves, nine deaths would bring me no regret.
I resent the king's wild recklessness, he never understands my loyal heart.
Women envy my moth-eyebrow beauty, spread lies that I am wanton, base.
The world excels in cunning tricks, turns from right rules to change measures.
Turning from straight lines to crooked curves, competing in flattery as their rule.
Downcast, sorrowful and distressed, alone I bear such hardship now.
I'd rather die and vanish at once, than adopt vulgar sycophantic ways.
The eagle flocks not with common birds, this has been true since ancient times.
How can square and round fit together? How can different minds live in peace?
I bow my heart and repress my will, endure blame and bear humiliation.
Preserving purity, dying for the right, ancient sages truly valued this.
I regret seeing not my path clearly, hesitate and now will turn my chariot.
Turn my carriage to retrace my road, before I wander too far astray.
Walk my horse by the orchid stream, rest on the hill of pepper trees.
Since advancement brings condemnation, retire to mend my former attire.
Make a coat of green lotus leaves, sew a skirt of white lotus blossoms.
Let none understand me if they will, so long as my heart remains fragrant.
Raise my cap to tower high above, lengthen my pendants to sway with grace.
Fragrance and radiance mingle together, my pure bright spirit remains unblemished.
Suddenly turn my head to gaze afar, resolve to roam four corners of earth.
My pendants are rich in adornment, sweet fragrance spreads more widely still.
Each man has his own delights, I alone love virtue as my constant way.
E'en if my body be torn asunder, my heart can never be altered.
My sister Nü Xu, anxious and caring, warned me again: Gun was stubborn and perished on Yu Mountain wild.
Why must you speak frankly and love virtue, upholding such purity alone?
Rooms are filled with common weeds, yet you stand apart and wear them not.
We cannot explain to every door, who will come examine our true hearts?
The world sides together in cliques, why stand alone and heed not my words?
Following ancient sages to moderate my nature, my heart burns with indignation still.
Crossing Yuan and Xiang southward, I lay my cause before Emperor Shun: Qi stole Nine Bian and Nine Songs, indulged in wanton self-pleasure.
Thinking not of danger nor consequence, his son Wu Guan raised rebellion.
Hou Yi abandoned himself to hunting, fond of shooting the great foxes.
The reckless come to no good end, Han Zhuo slew him and took his wife.
Han Ao relied on o'erwhelming might, indulging passions without restraint.
Day after day he reveled forgetting self, until his head was severed from his neck.
Jie of Xia acted against all reason, calamity came down upon him.
Zhou of Shang minced his loyal ministers, Shang dynasty could not endure.
Tang and Yu were reverent and solemn, early Zhou followed the Way without error.
They raised the worthy and employed the able, observing rules without partiality.
High Heaven is impartial in all things, sees virtue and lends its support.
Only sages of true noble virtue, may possess the lands beneath the sky.
I look back through hist'ry and forward, observe standards by which men judge things.
What unjust deed can ever be done?
What evil act can ever be practiced?
E'en facing death and mortal peril, looking back I feel no regret at all.
Shaping tenon without measuring socket, ancient sages were cruelly slain for this.
I heave long sighs and my tears stream, saddened I was born in ill-fated time.
Taking soft orchids to wipe my eyes, hot tears flow down and soak my garment.
I spread robes and kneel to state my case, having found the right way, my heart is clear.
Yoked to jade dragons, phoenix chariot borne, in whirlwind I ascend t'journey heav'nward.
At dawn I depart from Cangwu Mountain, at eve reach Xuanpu on Mount Kunlun.
I wish to linger at the spirit gate, but sun hastens west and dusk falls fast.
I bid Xi He slow her chariot pace, not rush toward Mount Yanzi as she nears.
The road before me is long and far, I'll search high and low for my heart's desire.
Water my dragons at Xianchi Pool, tie my reins on Fusang mulberry tree.
Break a Ruo branch to shade the sun, wander there freely for a little while.
Ahead moon goddess Wang Shu leads the way, behind wind god Fei Lian follows fast.
Luan birds and phoenixes clear the path, but Thunder Lord says all is not ready.
I command phoenixes to soar on wings, flying onward day and night without cease.
Whirlwinds gather and swirl around me, leading clouds and rainbows to welcome me.
Clouds and rainbows cluster, part, reunite, myriad colors shifting, rising, falling.
I bid heav'n's gatekeeper open his gate, but he leans 'gainst the door and stares coldly.
Light fades and evening darkens sky, I plait orchid garlands and wait long.
The world is foul, knows not worth from waste, loves to envy virtue, t'obscure excellence.
At dawn I'll cross the White Water River, climb Langfeng Peak and tether my horses.
Looking back suddenly my tears flow free, lamenting that on high hill there's no goddess.
I hasten to the palace of the Green Emperor, break a jade branch to lengthen my pendant.
Before blossoms fade and fall, seek a maiden below to receive my gift.
I command Feng Long to ride the clouds, to seek where goddess Fu Fei makes her home.
Loosening my girdle to send as pledge, I ask Jian Xiu to act as my matchmaker.
Clouds gather and swirl in profusion, but Fu Fei is perverse and hard to persuade.
At night she returns to Qiongshi to rest, at dawn washes hair at Weipan stream.
Proud of her beauty, arrogant, she revels day after day in wanton pleasure.
Though beautiful she lacks propriety, I abandon her and seek elsewhere.
I gaze across four corners of vast earth, descend after roaming across the heavens.
Behold the lofty Terrace of Jasper, I see Jian Di, fair maid of Yousong clan.
I bid the pois'nous dove to be my envoy, it tells me Jian Di is not good and true.
The male turtledove flies to matchmake, I find him too frivolous, full of false words.
My heart hesitates in indecision, wishing to go myself yet deeming it wrong.
The phoenix has already taken betrothal gifts, I fear Gao Xin has preceded me in winning her.
Thinking of wand'ring far but finding no rest, I wander idly roaming here and there.
Before Shao Kang has taken him a wife, there remain two princesses of the Yu clan.
My envoy is feeble and my words clumsy, I fear the match will not be secured.
The age is foul and envies worthy men, delighting to obscure virtue and exalt vice.
Beauties in chambers are unreachable, the wise king never wakens t'understanding.
I hold loyal heart with no outlet, how can I endure thus until life's end?
I take sacred herbs and bamboo slips, ask Ling Fen to divine my fortune.
He says: Two beauties must surely unite, but who is truly pure and worthy of love?
Consider how vast the world is, can beauteous women exist only in this land?
Go forth and doubt not, who seeks beauty would ever pass you by?
Where are there no fragrant plants? Why cling so stubbornly to your old home?
The world is dark and men's eyes are blinded, who can discern our good and evil?
Men's likes and dislikes differ, these men are stranger than all others!
They wear stinking mugwort at their waists, say delicate orchids are unfit to wear.
They cannot tell plants from one another, how can they judge precious jade correctly?
They fill their sachets with dung and filth, say Sichuan pepper has no true fragrance.
I wish to follow Ling Fen's auspice, yet my heart hesitates full of doubt.
I hear Wu Xian will descend at dusk, I carry pepper and rice to meet him.
The hundred gods descend in radiant procession, spirits of Jiu Yi come thronging t'welcome.
Wu Xian glows with numinous brightness, tells me tales of meetings of lord and minister.
He says: Strive to search high and low, seek one whose principles accord with yours.
Tang and Yu earnestly sought worthy ministers, Yi Yin and Gao Yao joined them in harmony.
If your heart truly loves cultivation, what need for matchmakers and go-betweens?
Fu Yue labored building walls at Fu Yan, Wu Ding employed him without slightest doubt.
Lü Wang was once a butcher in the market, King Wen found him and made him Preceptor.
Ning Qi sang while feeding oxen, Duke Huan heard him and took him as minister.
Act before your years have fully aged, before your appointed time has run out.
Fear lest the cuckoo cry too early, making all hundred herbs lose their fragrance.
Why is my jade pendant so surpassing fair, that men should obscure and hide it away?
These men are faithless and full of falsehood, fearing envy they will break and destroy it.
The times are chaos, shifting, changing, how can I linger here for long?
Orchids and angelica have lost fragrance, pollia have turned to common reeds.
Why have these fragrant plants of old, turned today to worthless weeds of the field?
Is there any other reason? 'Tis harm wrought by failing to cultivate virtue!
I once thought the orchid was reliable, but it proves false, empty of substance.
Abandoning virtue to follow the crowd, 'tis shaming to see it 'mong the fragrant.
Pepper grows cunning, flatt'ring, arrogant, thornbush strives to fill the sachet.
They press and push to gain advancement, how can they value true fragrance?
Such is the vulgar way, drifting with current, who can remain unchanging in this world?
Seeing pepper and orchid change thus, how much more the lesser common plants?
Only my jade pendant remains truly precious, its beauty rejected by all until this day.
Its rich fragrance cannot be dispelled, its scent lingers still, undiminished.
I maintain harmony and find pleasure, wand'ring forth to seek the beauty I desire.
While my pendant is still bright, resplendent, I'll range high and low to search the world.
Ling Fen has given auspicious divination, I choose a lucky day to start my journey.
I break jade tree branches for my food, grind fine jade dust as provisions for the road.
Flying dragons are harnessed to my chariot, adorned with ivory and jade in fine array.
How can hearts at odds dwell together?
I will go far away, estranged from them all.
I turn my course toward Kunlun Mountains, the road is long as I wander and observe.
Clouds and rainbows rise t'obscure the sun, jade bells ring with clear celestial sound.
At dawn I depart from Ford of Heaven, at evening reach the uttermost western end.
Phoenixes spread wings bearing banners, flying on high in solemn stately flight.
Suddenly I find myself in shifting sands, following Red River I wander slowly on.
I bid dragons form a bridge across the ford, summon Western Sov'reign to ferry me across.
The road is long and fraught with perils, I command retinues to wait by the road.
Passing Mount Buzhou I turn to the left, making Western Sea my appointed goal.
I gather a thousand chariots around me, jade wheels aligned to race forward together.
Eight dragons draw my chariot winding on, cloud banners flutter and stream in the wind.
I calm my spirit and slow my pace, thoughts soar aloft to the distant clouds.
I perform Nine Songs and dance Shao Dance, seizing this moment to find fleeting joy.
As my ancestors' radiance rises bright, I suddenly catch sight of my old homeland.
My servants grieve and my horses long for home, they turn back heads and will not go forward.
Envoi: It is finished!
Since none within the kingdom knows me, why should I long for my native capital?
Since none will join me in righteous rule, I'll go to join Peng Xian in his dwelling place!
tr:
我是上古帝王高阳氏的后裔，我伟大的先父名叫伯庸。
岁星在寅那年孟春正月庚寅之日，我降生到人间。
父亲观察我的生辰卦象，赐我美名正则，表字叫灵均。
我既有这么多内在美质，又不断加强修养。
我披挂着江离和辟芷，把秋兰编织成佩带。
时光如急流飞逝我追赶不上，岁月不等人令我心慌。
早晨在山坡采集木兰，傍晚在小洲摘取宿莽。
时光迅速逝去不能久留，四季更相代谢变化有常。
想到草木已由盛到衰，恐怕自己身体也逐渐衰老。
何不趁壮年抛弃污秽行径？为什么不改变这种不善法度？
乘上骏马纵横驰骋吧，我来在前面为你带路！
从前三王德行纯粹完美，众多贤臣都聚集在他们周围。
那里杂生着申椒和菌桂，哪里只是蕙草香芷连成佩带？
唐尧虞舜多么光明正大，沿着正道登上了坦途。
夏桀殷纣多么狂妄邪恶，贪图捷径最终走投无路。
结党营私的人苟且享乐，前途黑暗而充满险阻。
难道我害怕招灾惹祸吗？我只担心国家为此倾覆。
我前前后后奔走照料，希望能赶上前王的足迹。
君王不体察我一片赤诚，反而听信谗言对我发怒。
我本知忠言直谏会招祸患，想忍耐却还是止不住要说。
我指着苍天作证，这一切都是为了君王的缘故。
当初说好了黄昏为期，谁知道君王中途改了路！
当初君王已与我约定，后来又反悔改变了主意。
我并不难于与君王别离，只是伤心他的态度反复无常。
我栽培了九畹春兰，又种植了百亩秋蕙。
分垄栽培留夷和揭车，还套种了杜衡与芳芷。
希望它们枝繁叶茂高大挺拔，等成熟时节我就收割。
即使枯萎凋零又有何妨，最痛心众芳草荒芜变质。
小人们争权夺利贪得无厌，搜刮财物永远没有满足。
宽恕自己猜忌别人，勾心斗角互相嫉妒。
像奔马一样追逐私利，这不是我心中急着要做的事。
衰老渐渐向我逼近，我担心美名不能树立。
早晨饮用木兰花上坠落的露水，晚上咀嚼秋菊初开的花瓣。
只要我情感坚贞品质美好，长期面黄肌瘦又有何妨。
用木兰根须系上白芷，再把薜荔花蕊串连起来。
举起菌桂联结蕙草，把胡绳搓得修长美丽。
我效法古代前贤的装束，不与世俗小人服饰相同。
虽不合今人的习惯，我愿依照彭咸留下的榜样。
长长叹息掩面流泪，哀伤人民生活多灾多难。
我虽爱好修洁严于律己，早晨进谏晚上就被罢官。
他们攻击我佩带蕙草，又指责我爱好采集芳芷。
这是我心中追求的东西，就算多次死亡也不后悔。
怨愤君王实在荒唐放纵，始终不能体察我的忠心。
众女嫉妒我的蛾眉，造谣说我善于淫邪。
世俗本来善于投机取巧，违背规矩随意改变措施。
违背准绳追求邪曲，争着把苟合取容当作法度。
我烦闷忧愁失意不安，此时只有我独自遭受困厄。
宁可马上死去魂魄离散，也绝不做媚俗取巧的姿态。
雄鹰不与凡鸟同群，从古以来就是如此。
方与圆怎么能相合？志向不同怎么能相安无事？
委屈自己的心志，压抑自己的情感。
忍受责骂和侮辱，保持清白之志死于直道。
这本来就是前代圣贤所推崇的。
后悔当初没看清前途，迟疑一阵我要回头。
掉转车马回到原路，趁迷路还不算太远。
打马在兰草水边行走，跑上椒木小山暂且停留。
既然进取不成反而获罪，就退回来重整当初的服饰。
裁剪碧绿荷叶做上衣，缝缀洁白荷花做下裳。
没人了解我也就罢了，只要我内心真正馥郁芳柔。
把帽子加得高高耸立，把佩带加得悠长飘逸。
芳香与光泽杂糅在一起，我光明纯洁的品质没有亏损。
忽然回过头来放眼远眺，打算去四面八方观览周游。
佩带缤纷繁多装饰华丽，馥郁香气散发得更加浓烈。
人生各有各的乐趣，我独爱好修洁习以为常。
姐姐女嬃缠绵关切，反复告诫我说：鲧因刚直不顾性命，最终死在羽山荒野。
你为什么忠言直谏爱好修洁，独有你坚守这么多美好节操？
满屋都是普通花草，你却与众不同不肯佩带。
众人无法挨家挨户说明，谁会来体察我们的本心？
世人都互相吹捧成群结党，你为什么孤孤单单不听我的话？
依照前代圣贤道理节制性情，满腔忠愤至今不能平静。
渡过沅水湘水向南走去，我要向虞舜诉说衷情：夏启偷来九辩九歌，只顾放纵享乐。
不顾虑危难不考虑后果，五观因此发动了内乱。
后羿沉溺游猎玩乐，特别喜欢射杀大狐狸。
淫乱之徒本来没有好下场，寒浞杀了后羿霸占他的妻子。
寒浇自恃力气强大多么嚣张，放纵情欲不肯节制自己。
天天寻欢作乐忘乎所以，他的头颅因此掉落在地。
夏桀行为总违背常理，灾祸也就降临到他身上。
纣王把忠臣剁成肉酱，商朝国运因此不能长久。
商汤夏禹处事严肃恭敬，周初讲求正道没有差错。
举拔贤才任用能人，遵守规矩一点也不偏颇。
上天对一切公正无私，见有德之人就给予扶持帮助。
只有圣明德行高尚之人，才能享有天下的土地。
回顾前朝瞻望后代，观察人民衡量事情的标准。
哪有不义的事可以去干？
哪有不善的事可以去做？
即使面临死亡置身险境，回想当初志向我也毫不后悔。
不度量凿眼就削正榫头，前代贤人因此被剁成肉酱。
长声叹息泪流满面，哀伤我生不逢时如此不幸。
拿起柔软蕙草擦拭眼泪，热泪滚滚沾湿了我的衣襟。
铺开衣襟跪着慢慢陈述，我找到了正道心里明白。
驾着玉龙乘上凤车，风尘仆仆我将要上天远行。
清晨从苍梧山启程，傍晚就到达昆仑山上的悬圃。
想在灵琐稍作停留，太阳匆匆西沉暮色将至。
命令羲和慢些赶车，望见崦嵫山不要急于靠近。
前面的路漫长又遥远，我将要上天下地到处寻觅。
让马在咸池饮水，把马缰绳拴在扶桑树上。
折下若木枝条遮挡太阳，姑且在这里自由自在徜徉。
前面让月神望舒开路，后面让风神飞廉跟从奔忙。
鸾鸟凤凰在前面警戒，雷师却说还没有安排妥当。
命令凤凰展翅飞腾，要日日夜夜不停飞翔。
旋风聚集连结在一起，率领云霓前来迎接。
云霓越聚越多忽离忽合，五光十色上下飘浮荡漾。
叫天帝守门人把门打开，他却倚着天门冷冷把我观望。
日光渐暗天色将晚，我编结着幽兰久久伫立。
世道混乱污浊不分贤愚，喜欢嫉妒别人的美德抹煞长处。
清晨我将要渡过白水河，登上阆风山把马拴住。
忽然回头眺望涕泪涟涟，哀叹高丘上竟然没有神女。
匆匆来到春神青帝宫，折下琼枝系在佩带上。
趁着鲜花还没有凋落，去寻找下界可以接受馈赠的美人。
命令云神丰隆驾起云彩，去寻找宓妃居住的地方。
解下佩带束好书信，请蹇修前去为我做媒。
云霓纷纷簇集聚散离合，宓妃态度乖戾难以说合。
晚上宓妃回到穷石过夜，清晨她在洧盘水边洗发梳妆。
宓妃自恃美貌骄傲自大，整天寻欢作乐恣意游荡。
她虽然美丽却十分无礼，我放弃她改做别的追求。
览观四面八方遥远之地，周游天空之后我降临下界。
望见高耸巍峨的瑶台，看见有娀氏的美女简狄。
请鸩鸟前去为我做媒，鸩鸟却告诉我说简狄不好。
雄鸠叫唤着飞去说媒，我又嫌它太轻佻花言巧语。
心中犹豫迟疑不决，想自己去又觉得不合礼义。
凤凰已接受了聘礼，恐怕高辛氏已经抢先迎娶。
想到远方去又无处安居，只好四处游荡流浪逍遥。
趁着少康还没有成家，有虞氏还留着两位姚姓姑娘。
媒人笨拙口才又差，恐怕说合不能稳固牢靠。
世道浑浊嫉妒贤能，喜好遮蔽美德宣扬恶行。
闺中美人如此难以接近，贤明君王又始终不肯醒悟。
怀着一腔衷情无处抒发，我怎么能忍受这样到老！
找来灵草和细竹片，请灵氛为我占卜吉凶。
灵氛说：双方都美好必定能结合，但谁真正修洁值得爱慕？
想想天下这么广阔远大，难道只有这里才有美女吗？
努力远游不要疑惑，哪个寻求美女的人会放过你？
世间哪里没有芳草，为什么苦苦眷恋故园？
世道黑暗使人眼光迷乱，谁能辨别我们的善恶？
人们好恶本来就不相同，只是这帮小人特别古怪。
把艾草挂满腰间，反而说幽兰不可佩带。
连草木美恶都辨别不清，对美玉怎么能做出正确评价？
取来粪土塞满自己的香囊，反而说申椒一点也不芬芳。
想听从灵氛吉祥的占卜，心里却犹豫迟疑不决。
听说巫咸将在傍晚降神，我带着花椒香米前去迎候。
百神遮天蔽日一齐降临，九嶷山众神纷纷前去迎接。
巫咸灵光四射显示神异，告诉我往日君臣遇合的故事。
应该努力上天下地寻求，去寻找意气相投的同道知己。
商汤夏禹严谨求访贤臣，伊尹皋陶就能与他们协调和合。
只要内心真正爱好修洁，何必一定要靠媒人撮合说合？
傅说在傅岩筑墙劳作，武丁重用他毫不怀疑。
吕望曾经做过屠夫，遇到周文王就被举用为太师。
宁戚喂牛时敲牛角唱歌，齐桓公听了请他辅佐国政。
趁着年岁还没有衰老，时机也还没有完全丧失殆尽。
只怕杜鹃鸟叫得太早，使得百草都失去芬芳香气。
为什么我的玉佩这么高贵美丽，人们却要把它遮蔽埋藏？
这帮小人不讲信用，恐怕出于嫉妒要把它折断毁伤。
时世纷乱变化无常，我怎么能在这里长久停留？
兰草和芷草失去了芬芳，荃草和蕙草变成了茅草。
为什么往日的这些香草，今天都变成了荒野的蒿艾？
难道还有别的缘故吗？这是不好修洁造成的祸害。
原以为兰草可以依靠，谁知它华而不实虚有其表。
抛弃美德追随世俗，勉强列入众芳实在让人羞愧。
椒草专横谄媚傲慢自大，樧草又想充入香囊冒充芬芳。
它们拼命钻营追求权位，又怎么能敬重芬芳美德？
本来世俗风气就是随波逐流，又有谁能不发生变化？
看到椒兰尚且变成这样，何况揭车江离这些普通芳草？
只有我的玉佩最可贵，它的美质被人抛弃一直到今。
浓郁的香气难以消散，芬芳至今还没有完全消褪。
保持香气和欢愉自得其乐，姑且飘游四方寻求美女。
趁着玉佩还鲜丽华美，我要上天下地四处观览寻访。
灵氛已告诉我吉祥的占辞，选个吉日我将要启程远行。
折下玉树枝条作为珍馐，精磨玉屑作为旅途的干粮。
为我驾起飞龙，用美玉和象牙装饰我的车乘。
心志不同怎么能共处？
我将远走高飞自动疏远他们。
把行程转向昆仑山下，路途遥远继续周游观览。
云霞虹霓飞扬遮住阳光，车上玉铃叮当作响声震云天。
清晨从天河渡口出发，傍晚就到达了西方的尽头。
凤凰展开翅膀承托旌旗，高高飞翔整齐庄严。
忽然走到了流沙地带，沿着赤水道路从容徘徊。
指挥蛟龙在渡口架设桥梁，招呼西皇渡我过河去。
路途遥远又充满艰险，传令众车在路旁等待。
经过不周山向左转去，目标直指西海作为约会之地。
聚集了千辆战车，玉制车轮并排齐驱向前。
驾车的八龙蜿蜒前进，车上云旗随风舒卷飘扬。
定下心来慢慢前行，神思驰骋飞向遥远云天。
演奏《九歌》跳起《韶》舞，姑且借此时光寻找欢乐。
升起皇祖的灵光普照，忽然看到了我的故乡。
仆从悲伤马也怀恋，退缩回头不肯走向前方。
尾声：算了吧！
国内既然没有人了解我，又何必苦苦思念故国故都！
既然没有人能和我共行美政，我将追随彭咸到他居住的地方！
bg: 《离骚》为先秦代屈原所作。先秦时期是中国诗歌的发轫时代，《诗经》的现实主义与《楚辞》的浪漫主义共同奠定了中国诗歌的优良传统，四言为主，重章叠句，一唱三叹。作者屈原在这一时期的创作，多与其人生际遇、时代背景紧密相关，作品亦承载了特定情境下的情志与感怀。

appr:
《离骚》艺术赏析

《离骚》是战国时期楚国诗人屈原的代表作，是中国古代最长的抒情诗，也是中国浪漫主义文学的奠基之作，被誉为"辞赋之宗""千古万古至奇之作"。全诗共373句，2490字，以诗人的身世、志向、遭遇为线索，将个人身世、国家命运、政治理想、人生追求熔于一炉，结构宏伟，想象奇特，情感充沛，文辞瑰丽，是中国文学史上光耀千古的不朽名篇。

一、历代权威评点

- 司马迁《史记·屈原贾生列传》："其文约，其辞微，其志洁，其行廉，其称文小而其指极大，举类迩而见义远。其志洁，故其称物芳；其行廉，故死而不容。自疏濯淖污泥之中，蝉蜕于浊秽，以浮游尘埃之外，不获世之滋垢，皭然泥而不滓者也。推此志也，虽与日月争光可也。"
- 刘勰《文心雕龙·辨骚》："自《风》《雅》寝声，莫或抽绪，奇文郁起，其《离骚》哉！固已轩翥诗人之后，奋飞辞家之前，岂去圣之未远，而楚人之多才乎！""观其骨鲠所树，肌肤所附，虽取熔经意，亦自铸伟辞……故能气往轹古，辞来切今，惊采绝艳，难与并能矣。"
- 李白《江上吟》："屈平词赋悬日月，楚王台榭空山丘。"
- 鲁迅《汉文学史纲要》："战国之世，在韵言则有屈原起于楚，被谗放逐，乃作《离骚》。逸响伟辞，卓绝一世。后人惊其文采，相率仿效，以原楚产，故称'楚辞'。较之于《诗》，则其言甚长，其思甚幻，其文甚丽，其旨甚明，凭心而言，不遵矩度。故后儒之服膺诗教者，或訾而绌之，然其影响于后来之文章，乃甚或在三百篇以上。"

二、三大艺术特色

第一，**宏伟壮丽的结构**。《离骚》规模宏大，结构严谨，全诗分为三大部分：第一部分从开篇到"固前圣之所厚"，自叙身世、修身立志、忠而被谤、九死不悔，是对现实遭遇的抒写；第二部分从"悔相道之不察兮"到"余焉能忍与此终古"，是奇幻的想象世界——女嬃劝诫、陈词重华、上下求索、三次求女，是在幻想中对理想的追求；第三部分从"索藑茅以筳篿兮"到结尾，灵氛占卜、巫咸劝行、远游西极、临睨旧乡、以死明志，是理想最终破灭后的抉择。全诗波澜壮阔，跌宕起伏，从现实到幻想，再从幻想回到现实，结构完整，层次分明，是一首气势磅礴的宏伟史诗。

第二，**瑰丽奇特的浪漫想象**。屈原在《离骚》中突破了现实时空的限制，驱遣神话传说中的人物——羲和（太阳神）、望舒（月神）、飞廉（风神）、雷师、丰隆（云神）、帝阍（天门守卫），驾龙御凤，乘风上天，饮马咸池，系马扶桑，登阆风，游春宫，求宓妃，觅简狄，上下四方求索，天上地下遨游，创造了一个无比瑰丽奇幻的浪漫世界。这种大胆奇特的想象，开创了中国浪漫主义诗歌的传统，后世李白、李贺、苏轼等浪漫主义诗人无不受其滋养。

第三，**系统完整的香草美人象征体系**。屈原在《离骚》中创造了中国诗歌史上第一个完整的象征体系——"香草美人"体系：以香草（江离、辟芷、秋兰、木兰、宿莽、申椒、菌桂、蕙、茝、芰荷、芙蓉等二十余种香草）象征高洁的品格和贤能的人才；以恶草（萧、艾、樧等）象征奸邪的小人和变节之人；以美人（灵修、蛾眉、众女、宓妃、简狄、二姚）象征君主和理想中的知音；以男女爱情、婚娶比喻君臣际遇；以"众女嫉余之蛾眉"比喻群小嫉妒贤臣。这一象征体系影响了中国文学两千多年，从张衡《四愁诗》、曹植《洛神赋》，到李商隐无题诗、辛弃疾婉约词，无不继承了这一比兴传统。

三、情感深度与精神力量

《离骚》最打动人心的是屈原深沉真挚的爱国情怀和九死不悔的气节精神。"长太息以掩涕兮，哀民生之多艰"，是对人民疾苦的深切同情；"亦余心之所善兮，虽九死其犹未悔"，是对理想信念的坚定执着；"路漫漫其修远兮，吾将上下而求索"，是对真理不懈追求的精神；"既莫足与为美政兮，吾将从彭咸之所居"，是理想破灭后以死殉道的气节。这种精神已经融入中华民族的文化血脉，成为中国知识分子精神传统的重要源头。

《离骚》起承转合章法结构分析

《离骚》全诗373句，篇幅宏大，按照情感发展的脉络，可以分为八大段，起承转合章法完备，层次分明，结构严谨：

【第一段·起：自叙身世·修身立志】
从"帝高阳之苗裔兮"到"来吾道夫先路"，共24句。
起笔高远，从自己的族源、家世、生辰、美名写起，表明自己出身高贵、禀赋内美，又注重后天修养，博采众善，修身立德，急切地想要辅佐君主、实现美政理想。开篇气势不凡，为全诗奠定了崇高悲壮的基调。

【第二段·承：忠而被谤·党人误国】
从"昔三后之纯粹兮"到"伤灵修之数化"，共32句。
承接开篇志向，对比三王尧舜的清明与桀纣党人的昏庸，写自己忠心耿耿奔走效力，反而被谗见疏，君主反复无常，党人苟且偷安，国家前途危殆。这一段是对现实政治遭遇的直接抒写，矛盾冲突初现。

【第三段·转：九死不悔·坚守节操】
从"余既滋兰之九畹兮"到"愿依彭咸之遗则"，共40句。
笔锋一转，从批评朝政转向抒写个人志向：自己虽然培养的人才变节，虽然被罢官免职，虽然被众人诽谤，但只要是心中认定的美好理想，"虽九死其犹未悔"，宁死也不与奸邪小人同流合污。这一段是屈原气节精神的集中体现，"亦余心之所善兮，虽九死其犹未悔"成为千古名句。

【第四段·承：长太息掩涕·忧国忧民】
从"长太息以掩涕兮"到"固前圣之所厚"，共28句。
再承前意，"长太息以掩涕兮，哀民生之多艰"，抒发对民生疾苦的深切同情和对群小当权的愤慨，表明自己"伏清白以死直"的决心，宁可牺牲生命也绝不改变节操。这一段情感沉郁悲壮，将忧国忧民之情推向第一个高潮。

【第五段·转：上下求索·三次求女】
从"悔相道之不察兮"到"余焉能忍与此终古"，共76句。
是全诗最具浪漫色彩的核心段落。诗人在现实中完全失望，转而进入幻想世界：先有女嬃劝诫，他不听；于是向重华陈词，得到了精神上的肯定；然后驾龙飞腾，上天入地，开始"上下求索"——令羲和弭节、望舒先驱、飞廉奔属，叩天阍天门不开，求宓妃高傲无礼，寻简狄媒人无能，觅二姚犹豫软弱，三次求女全部失败，象征着在楚国寻求明君、实现美政的理想彻底破灭。"路漫漫其修远兮，吾将上下而求索"就在这一段，是全诗精神的核心。

【第六段·承：灵氛占卜·巫咸劝行】
从"索藑茅以筳篿兮"到"周流观乎上下"，共56句。
三次求女失败后，诗人请灵氛占卜，灵氛劝他离国远游，去别的国家寻求贤君；他犹豫不决，又请巫咸降神，巫咸举傅说遇武丁、吕望遇文王、宁戚遇齐桓公的故事，劝他趁年华未老及时远行，不要犹豫错过时机。这一段写诗人内心的矛盾挣扎：去国还是留楚？是全诗情感的又一转折。

【第七段·合：远游西极·临睨旧乡】
从"灵氛既告余以吉占兮"到"蜷局顾而不行"，共64句。
诗人终于决定听从灵氛的劝告，择日远行，驾飞龙、乘瑶车、扬云霓、鸣玉鸾，遨游天空，远游西极，"奏《九歌》而舞《韶》兮，聊假日以媮乐"，在光明的太空中自由翱翔，这是全诗浪漫想象的最高潮。然而，就在他升上光明的高空、即将远离楚国的时候——"忽临睨夫旧乡"，忽然低头看见了自己的故乡楚国！"仆夫悲余马怀兮，蜷局顾而不行"，仆人悲伤，马也留恋，都不肯再往前走。这是全诗最震撼人心的转折：千回百转，终究不忍离开自己的祖国。

【第八段·终章：乱曰明志·以死殉道】
最后5句（乱曰）："已矣哉！国无人莫我知兮，又何怀乎故都！既莫足与为美政兮，吾将从彭咸之所居！"
尾声收束全篇，是全诗情感的最终落点：算了吧！国内没有人了解我，我又何必怀念故都？既然没有人能和我一起实现美政理想，我将追随彭咸，以死明志！这五句沉郁悲壮，掷地有声，点明了全诗的主旨，也预示了屈原后来投汨罗江殉国的人生结局，余韵悠长，震撼千古。

全诗八大段，起承转合自然流畅，从现实到幻想，再从幻想回到现实，从立志到失意，从求索到彷徨，从远游到殉国，情感脉络清晰，结构完整圆融，达到了抒情诗结构艺术的最高成就。

《离骚》意象体系解读：香草美人，浪漫瑰奇

《离骚》创造了中国诗歌史上最完整、最系统的意象体系——"香草美人"体系，这一体系贯穿全诗，成为楚辞艺术的核心特征，影响了中国文学两千多年。

一、香草意象群：高洁品格的象征

屈原在《离骚》中写了二十余种香草，构成了一个完整的香草意象群，每一种香草都有其特定的象征意义：
- **江离、辟芷、秋兰**："扈江离与辟芷兮，纫秋兰以为佩"，这是屈原修身的象征，披香草、佩秋兰，比喻自己博采众善，修养高洁品格。江离、白芷、泽兰都是楚地常见的芳香植物，生长在水边山野，清香高洁，用来比喻君子的美德。
- **木兰、宿莽**："朝搴阰之木兰兮，夕揽洲之宿莽"，木兰去皮不死，宿莽经冬不枯，象征着坚贞不屈、经得住考验的品格。
- **申椒、菌桂、蕙、茝**："昔三后之纯粹兮，固众芳之所在。杂申椒与菌桂兮，岂惟纫夫蕙茝"，这些都是香草，比喻前代贤君朝堂上众多贤能的人才。
- **芰荷、芙蓉**："制芰荷以为衣兮，集芙蓉以为裳"，菱叶和荷花，出淤泥而不染，象征着诗人高洁的品格，不与世俗同流合污。

与之相对的是恶草意象：
- **萧、艾、樧（茱萸）**："兰芷变而不芳兮，荃蕙化而为茅。何昔日之芳草兮，今直为此萧艾也？"原本的香草变成了萧艾等恶草，比喻诗人培养的人才变节，投靠奸邪小人，道德堕落。

这一"香草恶草"的二元对立意象，开创了中国诗歌以物喻人的比兴传统，后世诗词中的梅兰竹菊"四君子"意象，正是渊源于此。

二、美人意象群：君臣际遇的比喻

"美人"是《离骚》另一核心意象群，同样形成了完整的体系：
- **灵修（美人）**：指楚怀王，是屈原忠爱的对象。"惟草木之零落兮，恐美人之迟暮"，以美人年华老去比喻君主昏庸误国，政治理想不能实现。
- **蛾眉（美女自喻）**："众女嫉余之蛾眉兮，谣诼谓余以善淫"，屈原以美貌女子自比，以女子的美貌比喻自己的美德才能，以"众女嫉蛾眉"比喻朝廷群小嫉妒自己的才能，造谣诽谤。
- **宓妃、简狄、二姚**：这三位是神话传说中的美女——洛水女神宓妃、商代祖先契的母亲简狄、夏代少康的妻子二姚。屈原"上下求索"三次求女，求宓妃因其"美而无礼"放弃，求简狄因媒人笨拙失败，求二姚因说理不深犹豫，三次求女全部失败，象征着诗人在楚国寻求贤君、知音、理想的政治际遇的失败。
- **佚女**：指美女，理想的知音。"哀高丘之无女""相下女之可诒"，多次寻求美人而不得，是诗人政治理想无法实现的象征。

这种以男女爱情比喻君臣际遇的手法，是屈原的伟大创造，它将政治情感转化为男女情爱，使抽象的政治情感具象化、情感化，更加真挚动人，影响了后世无数诗人。

三、神话意象群：浪漫世界的建构

为了实现"上下求索"的浪漫想象，屈原驱遣了大量神话人物和神话地理意象，建构了一个宏大瑰丽的神话世界：
- **日月风云神**：羲和（太阳神驾车者）、望舒（月神驾车者）、飞廉（风神）、丰隆（云神/雷神），这些神话人物都为诗人服务，听他指挥。
- **昆仑神话系统**：咸池（太阳沐浴处）、扶桑（太阳升起处的神树）、若木（太阳落下处的神树）、崦嵫（太阳落下的山）、阆风（昆仑山的山峰）、白水（昆仑山上的神水）、春宫（东方青帝所居），构成了诗人升天遨游的广阔空间。
- **神巫意象**：灵氛、巫咸，古代神巫，能通神占卜，沟通人神。
- **历史人物意象**：三后（禹汤文王）、尧舜、桀纣、齐桓公、傅说、吕望、宁戚、彭咸等历史人物，正反对比，作为诗人政治理想和人生抉择的参照。

这些神话意象共同构建了一个无比宏大瑰丽的浪漫世界，让《离骚》成为中国浪漫主义文学的源头。

四、道路意象：上下求索的人生之路

"路"是《离骚》中贯穿全篇的核心意象："来吾道夫先路""夫惟捷径以窘步""既遵道而得路""路漫漫其修远兮，吾将上下而求索"。这里的"路"既是现实中的道路，也是诗人的人生道路、政治道路、追求理想的道路。"路漫漫其修远兮，吾将上下而求索"之所以成为千古名句，正是因为它写出了所有追求真理、追求理想的人共同的心声。

《离骚》的香草美人意象体系不是零散的比喻，而是一个完整的、系统的象征世界，它将政治理想、人生追求、道德品格、情感志向全部熔铸在意象之中，开创了中国诗歌"托物言志""借景抒情"的艺术传统，成为后世诗人学习的典范。

title: 寻西山隐者不遇
author: 丘为
note: 《寻西山隐者不遇》是丘为的经典作品，语言凝练，意境深远，为历代读者所传诵。【寻西山隐者不遇】唐代丘为所作的诗。
tr: 絕頂一茅茨，直[上]三十里。扣關無僮僕，窺室唯案几。若非巾柴車，應是釣秋水。差池不相見，黽勉空仰止。草色新雨中，松聲晚牕裏。及茲契幽絕，自足蕩心耳。雖無賓主意，頗得清淨理。興盡方下山，何必待之子。
appr: 《寻西山隐者不遇》是唐代丘为所作的诗名篇。作品采用四言为主的句式，古朴厚重，直陈其事，是先秦古诗典型风格。艺术上，作品善于选取典型意象融情于景，用词精炼传神，于平淡处见深情，读来余韵悠长。作为唐代诗歌的经典篇章，《寻西山隐者不遇》历代传诵不衰，是丘为诗歌风格的集中体现。

【山】山峦意象，常象征巍峨、永恒、隐逸、阻隔。

【水】流水意象，喻时光流逝、离愁绵长，亦指壮阔胸怀。

【雨】雨意象，春雨喜，秋雨愁，夜雨乡思，暮雨离愁。

【草】草意象，春草生意，秋草萧瑟，常喻离愁与岁月。

诸意象交织呼应，共同构成完整的意境整体，使抽象情感具象可感。
bg: 《寻西山隐者不遇》为唐代丘为所作。唐代是中国诗歌的黄金时代，初唐四杰承先启后，盛唐李杜高岑王孟群星璀璨，中唐元白韩孟柳刘各擅胜场，晚唐小李杜温李余韵悠长，古近体各体皆备。作者丘为在这一时期的创作，多与其人生际遇、时代背景紧密相关，作品亦承载了特定情境下的情志与感怀。
theme: 《寻西山隐者不遇》主旨在于描绘自然山水之美，寄托隐逸或热爱自然之情。；写田园生活之趣，表达淡泊自适的人生志趣。作品以凝练的语言、鲜明的意象，将情感寄寓于景物与叙事之中，含蓄深沉，意蕴丰厚，千百年来引发读者广泛共鸣，是唐代丘为的代表性作品之一。

baihua_lines: 高高的山顶上盖着一座茅屋，
我走了三十里山路才来到这里。
敲门却没有僮仆出来应答，
往屋里看只有案几和桌椅。
他若不是驾着柴车出去游玩，
就是到秋水边钓鱼去了。
我这次终究没能和他相见，
白辜负了我这一番登山的诚意。
刚下过雨的山色青翠秀美，
沿着小路我走到了松树下。
他的庭院里沾着新雨的痕迹，
青苔上留着他走过的脚印。
和他相逢终究是没有缘分，
我对着这幽静的景色满怀怅惘。
我倒不如学他那样超然潇洒，
一辈子归隐在这山林之间。
baihua: 绝顶一茅茨，直[上]三十里。扣关无僮仆，窥室唯案几。若非巾柴车，应是钓秋水。差池不相见，黾勉空仰止。草色新雨中，松声晚牕里。及兹契幽绝，自足荡心耳。虽无宾主意，颇得清净理。兴尽方下山，何必待之子。
en_lines: Upon the highest peak stands a thatched cottage,
I walked thirty li of mountain path to reach it.
I knocked, but no serving boy came to answer,
Peering inside, I saw only desk and chair.
If he is not riding his rustic cart to wander the hills,
He must have gone to fish by the autumn waters.
After all, I have missed the chance to meet him,
My mountain climb was made in vain this day.
Fresh after rain, the mountain hues are green and fair,
Following the path I walk beneath the pine trees.
His courtyard still bears traces of recent showers,
Green moss retains the imprint of his footsteps.
To meet him was, after all, not destined,
I gaze on this quiet scene with wistful heart.
I would do better to learn his free and easy way,
And live as a hermit among these woods and hills forever.

author: 僧皎然

baihua_lines: 他把家迁到了城郭边上，
村野小路一直通向桑麻地。
篱笆边种着菊花却不见主人，
原来是秋天出去还没有回来。
敲门惊动了邻家的狗吠，
问邻居说他去西山了。
每天回来时太阳都已西斜，
知道他每天总是要到天黑才回家。
baihua: 移家虽带郭，野径入桑麻。近种篱边菊，秋来未著花。扣门无犬吠，欲去问西家。报道山中去，归时每日斜。
en_lines: He moved his home beside the city wall,
Village paths lead out through fields of hemp and mulberry.
Chrysanthemums bloom by the fence, but no master is seen,
He has gone out this autumn day and not yet returned.
My knock arouses the neighbor's dog to bark,
Asking, they say he has gone to the western hills.
Each day he returns when the sun slants low,
I know he never comes home until the dark of night.

baihua_lines: 空旷冷落的古老行宫，
只有宫花依然寂寞地开着。
几个满头白发的宫女，
闲坐着谈论唐玄宗的往事。
baihua: 寥落古行宫。宫花寂寞红。白头宫女在。闲坐说玄宗。
en_lines: Deserted and forlorn, the old imperial palace stands,
Only the palace flowers still bloom in lonely silence.
A few palace ladies with hair all turned to white,
Sit idly by, talking of the old days of Emperor Xuanzong.

baihua_lines: 想起你和我共过贫贱的日子已经一去不返，
今天你下葬之后我更是暗自伤神。
你生前穿过的衣裳眼看都快施舍完了，
你留下的针线盒我至今不忍心打开。
还念着你旧日待下人的恩情，
我也因为你而格外怜惜那些婢女。
我常常怀着和你死后同葬一穴的心愿，
也知道再结来世姻缘终究渺茫难期。
baihua: 谢公最小偏怜女，自嫁黔娄百事乖。顾我无衣搜荩箧，泥他沽酒拔金钗。野蔬充膳甘长藿，落叶添薪仰古槐。今日俸钱过十万，与君营奠复营斋。
en_lines: The days we shared in poverty are gone forever,
After your burial today, my grief grows deeper still.
The clothes you wore in life I have nearly given all away,
But I cannot bear to open your old sewing box.
Remembering your kindness to the servants in old days,
For your sake I show the maids special tenderness.
I often dream that we shall share a grave in death,
Though I know reunion in another life is a vain, distant hope.

title: 遣悲怀·其三
author: 元稹
note: 《遣悲怀·其三》是元稹的经典作品，语言凝练，意境深远，为历代读者所传诵。【遣悲怀·其三】唐代元稹所作的诗。

baihua_lines: 闲坐时为你悲伤，也为我自己叹息，
人生百年有多少事能够如人所愿？
邓攸没有儿子是命运的安排，
潘岳写悼亡诗也只是徒然悲戚。
即使死后合葬也无法倾诉衷肠，
来世结为夫妻更是渺茫无期。
只有整夜睁着眼睛思念你，
才能报答你生前为我受的清苦。
baihua: 闲坐悲君亦自悲，百年都是几多时。邓攸无子寻知命，潘岳悼亡犹费词。同穴窅冥何所望，他生缘会更难期。惟将终夜长开眼，报答平生未展眉。
en_lines: Sitting idly, I grieve for you and sigh for myself,
In a hundred years of life, how few things go as we wish?
Deng You was childless—it was fate's own doing,
Pan Yue wrote memorial poems, yet all his grief was vain.
Even sharing a grave in death cannot tell our hearts' full tale,
To be husband and wife in the next world is but a distant dream.
I can only lie awake all night thinking of you,
To repay the hardship you endured for me in life.

author: 元稹

baihua_lines: 从前我们开玩笑说过的身后事，
今天一件件都摆在我眼前。
你的衣裳已经施舍得快没了，
你留下的针线我还存着不忍打开。
还念着旧情我格外怜惜你从前的婢女，
我也曾因为梦见你而给人送钱财。
我知道夫妻死别的遗憾人人都有，
可想起我们贫贱时共度的日子就事事悲哀。
baihua: 昔日戏言身后意，今朝都到眼前来。衣裳已施行看尽，针线犹存未忍开。尚想旧情怜婢仆，也曾因梦送钱财。诚知此恨人人有，贫贱夫妻百事哀。
en_lines: What we once spoke of in jest, about what comes after death,
Today has all come true before my very eyes.
Your clothes are almost all given away to others,
Your needlework remains, but I cannot bear to open it.
Remembering old affection, I show kindness to your maids,
I have given money away after dreaming of you.
I know this grief of parting comes to every wedded couple,
But for us who shared dire poverty, every memory brings sorrow.

title: 石鱼湖上醉歌
author: 元结

baihua_lines: 石鱼湖像洞庭湖一样壮观，
公田的湖水漫山遍野。
夏天水涨仿佛君山浮在水上，
饮酒作乐正好消磨时光。
山当酒杯水当酒池，
大家喝得醉倒在小山上。
喝起酒来只觉得天久地长，
哪里知道人间的岁月时光。
我坐在石鱼湖上，
终日长醉不愿醒来。
baihua: 石鱼湖，似洞庭，夏水欲满君山青。山为樽，水为沼，酒徒历历坐洲岛。长风连日作大浪，不能废人运酒舫。我持长瓢坐巴丘，酌饮四坐以散愁。
en_lines: Stone Fish Lake is as grand as Dongting Lake,
Waters from the public fields spread across the hills.
In summer the waters rise as if Jun Mountain floats upon them,
We drink and make merry, letting time pass idly by.
Hills become our goblets, waters become our wine pool,
We drink until we lie drunken upon the little hill.
As we drink, heaven and earth seem everlasting,
We forget the passing years and months of mortal life.
I sit upon Stone Fish Lake,
Drunken all day long, unwilling to awake.

title: 贼退示官吏
author: 元结
note: 《贼退示官吏》是元结的经典作品，语言凝练，意境深远，为历代读者所传诵。【贼退示官吏】唐代元结所作的诗。
tr: 昔歲逢太平，山林二十年。泉源在庭戶，洞壑當門前。井稅有常期，日[晏]猶得眠。忽然遭世變，數歲親戎旃。今來典斯郡，山夷又紛然。城小賊不屠，人貧傷可憐。是以陷隣境，此州獨見全。使臣將王命，豈不如賊焉。今彼徴斂者，迫之如火煎。誰能絕人命，以作時世賢。思欲委符節，引竿自刺船。將家就魚麥，歸老江湖邊。

baihua_lines: 癸卯年，西原蛮贼攻入道州，
焚烧抢掠几乎把全城洗劫一空。
等到贼人退走之后，
朝廷派来的赋税使臣又接连而至。
横征暴敛的命令一道接一道，
我实在不忍心再逼迫苦难的百姓。
我写下这首诗给地方官吏们看。
从前遇到太平盛世，
我在山林里隐居了二十年。
泉水的源头就在我的院子里，
山谷山洞正对着我的门前。
官府征收赋税有固定的常例，
日子过得自在安闲。
等到世道大乱战争爆发，
我出来做官几次都赶上战乱。
如今我奉命来镇守这偏僻的山城，
山贼又来这里骚扰百姓。
城池太小贼人无心攻打，
百姓太穷他们也心生怜悯。
可朝廷派来的使臣奉命征收赋税，
难道还不如这些山贼吗？
那些横征暴敛的官吏们，
简直比猛虎和毒蛇还要凶狠。
（诗句：归老江湖边。）
baihua: 昔岁逢太平，山林二十年。泉源在庭户，洞壑当门前。井税有常期，日[晏]犹得眠。忽然遭世变，数岁亲戎旃。今来典斯郡，山夷又纷然。城小贼不屠，人贫伤可怜。是以陷隣境，此州独见全。使臣将王命，岂不如贼焉。今彼徴敛者，迫之如火煎。谁能绝人命，以作时世贤。思欲委符节，引竿自刺船。将家就鱼麦，归老江湖边。
en_lines: In the year guimao, the barbarian rebels of Xiyuan invaded Daozhou,
Burning, killing, and looting until the city was nearly laid waste.
After the rebels had withdrawn and gone,
Imperial tax commissioners came one after another.
Edicts for harsh levies and exactions arrived without cease,
I could not bear to press the suffering people further,
So I write this poem to show to my fellow officials.
Long ago, in the years of peace and prosperity,
I lived as a hermit in the hills for twenty years.
A spring had its source right within my courtyard,
Valleys and caves stood directly before my gate.
Taxes and levies followed fixed and regular schedules,
Days passed in quiet leisure and contentment.
Then came the troubles, wars broke out across the land,
When I took office, I met with rebellion time and again.
Now I am commanded to guard this remote mountain city,
And mountain bandits come to harass our people.
The town is too small for the rebels to bother capturing,
The people are so poor even bandits feel pity.
Yet the imperial commissioners, bearing royal edicts for taxes,
Are they not worse even than these rebel bandits?
Those who impose these cruel taxes and exactions,
Are more fierce than tigers, more venomous than snakes.
(Verse: 归老江湖边。)

title: 春怨
author: 刘方平
note: 《春怨》是刘方平的经典作品，语言凝练，意境深远，为历代读者所传诵。【春怨】唐代刘方平所作的诗。
tr: 紗窗日落漸黃昏，金屋無人見淚痕。寂寞空庭春欲晚，梨花滿地不開門。

author: 刘方平

The Dipper hangs sideways, the Southern Dipper tilts low.
Tonight for the first time I feel the warmth of spring,
As insect sounds newly filter through the green window gauze.

title: 阙题
author: 刘昚虚
note: 【流水】流动的水，常喻时光流逝、愁绪绵长。
【阙题】唐代刘昚虚所作的诗。
tr: 道由白雲盡，春與青溪長。時有落花至，遠隨流水香。閑門向山路，深柳讀書堂。幽映每白日，清輝照衣裳。

baihua_lines: 山路被白云隔断在尘世之外，
春日的芬芳悠悠地从早流到晚。
时常有落花随着流水漂出来，
远远就知道这山里有个仙境般的地方。
我静静对着溪水读书，
悠闲地靠着松树和人闲谈。
我的心向来就淡泊宁静，
在这清溪边洗耳，不听尘世的喧嚣。
baihua: 道由白云尽，春与青溪长。时有落花至，远随流水香。闲门向山路，深柳读书堂。幽映每白日，清辉照衣裳。
en_lines: The mountain path is cut off from the mortal world by white clouds,
Spring fragrance drifts slowly from morning until evening.
Fallen petals often float out upon the flowing stream,
From afar one knows there is a fairyland deep in these hills.
I sit quietly reading beside the brook,
Leisurely chatting with friends against a pine tree.
My heart has long been tranquil and free of desire,
I wash my ears in this clear stream, deaf to the world's noise.

Hearing songs upon the river, my heart shifts between joy and grief.
The sun shines in the east while rain falls in the west,
You say it is not clear weather, yet the sky is clear (qing—meaning love).

en_lines: Willows are fresh and green, the river flows calm and smooth,
I hear my beloved singing upon the river.
The sun shines in the east while rain falls in the west,
You say there is no clear weather (no love), yet there is (love).

baihua_lines: 先主刘备的英雄气概名传千古，
他的祠庙至今巍峨耸立在山中。
三国分立时他苦心经营蜀汉，
恢复汉室的志向最终没能实现。
得到诸葛亮这样的贤相真是如鱼得水，
生了刘禅那样的儿子实在不像父亲。
昔日蜀国的歌女如今归了魏国，
荒凉的蜀地故地只剩下祠庙供人凭吊。
baihua: 天地英雄气，千秋尚凛然。势分三足鼎，业复五铢钱。得相能开国，生儿不象贤。凄凉蜀故妓，来舞魏宫前。
en_lines: The heroic spirit of Emperor Liu Bei lives through the ages,
His temple still stands tall and grand among the hills.
In the age of Three Kingdoms he built the kingdom of Shu through toil,
But his dream to restore the Han house was never fulfilled.
Finding a minister like Zhuge Liang was like a fish finding water,
But begetting a son like Liu Shan, the heir did not take after his father.
The singing girls of old Shu are now in the kingdom of Wei,
Only the desolate shrine remains in the old land of Shu for mourners.

author: 刘禹锡

金陵的王气黯然失色。
千丈长的铁链沉入江底，
一片降旗从石头城上举了起来。
人世间多少次令人感伤的往事，
山形依旧枕靠着寒冷的江流。
如今四海一统天下太平，
旧日的营垒都隐没在萧萧芦荻中。
baihua: 西晋楼船下益州，金陵王气黯然收。千寻铁锁沈江底，一片降旛出石头。人世几回伤往事，山形依旧枕江流。今逢四海为家日，故垒萧萧芦荻秋。
en_lines: Wang Jun's warships sailed east downriver from Yizhou,
The royal aura of Jinling dimmed and faded away.
Thousand-zhang iron chains sank to the river bottom,
A banner of surrender was raised above Stone City.
How many sorrowful events have passed in this mortal world,
Yet the mountains still rest as ever against the cold river flow.
Now all within the four seas is unified and at peace,
The old fortresses lie hidden among the whispering reeds.

baihua_lines: 一路走去寻找常道士，
莓苔上留下了鞋印。
白云环绕着静谧的沙洲，

沿着山路来到溪水源头。

领悟了禅理心里已无世俗杂念。

en_lines: I walk along the path searching for the Daoist Chang,
Shoe prints are left upon the mossy stones.
White clouds encircle the quiet sandbar,
Green grass seals his peaceful, idle gate.
After fresh rain the pines are vivid green,
Following the mountain path I reach the river source.
Gazing at flowers reflected in the stream,
I attain Chan understanding—worldly thoughts are gone.

author: 刘长卿

en_body: In the cool chamber no outer sound intrudes,
The seven strings of Kongsang ring distinct and clear.
What I play is no fashionable new tune,
How could worldly ears deign to stop and hear?
The moon has set before the song ends,
In the dark the Xiang goddess seems to weep.
As if conveying the sorrow within my heart,
Like clouds over Cangwu a thousand li deep.

title: 新年作
author: 刘长卿
note: 《新年作》是刘长卿的经典作品，语言凝练，意境深远，为历代读者所传诵。【新年作】唐代刘长卿所作的诗。

en_body: My homesick heart grows more urgent at the new year,
At the edge of heaven alone my tears fall free.
Old age has come, yet I live beneath others,
Spring returns before this traveler can flee.
With mountain apes I pass both dawn and dusk,
With river willows I share mist and wind.
I am like Jia Yi, exiled to Changsha,
How many more years must I here remain?

在天涯我独自潸然落泪。

en_body: In this life I never expected to receive an imperial edict of grace,
Amid world's affairs I vainly learned to sing drunk in distress.
Over the river the moon is bright as wild geese fly past,
In Huainan leaves fall, and Chu's mountains seem numberless.
I rejoice to find shelter near Cangzhou's shores,
Yet gazing at my white hair there is naught I can do.
Now worn with age, discarded by all the world,
I am ashamed you still warn me to beware life's rough tide.

title: 秋日登吴公台上寺远眺
author: 刘长卿
note: 【秋日登吴公台上寺远眺】唐代刘长卿所作的诗。

en_body: After plants shed their leaves upon the ancient terrace,
In autumn daylight I gaze out with a homesick heart.
Few visitors come to this temple in the wilds,
Cloud-capped peaks are parted by waters deep and far apart.
The setting sun lingers upon the old ramparts,
Cold chime tones fill the empty woods all around.
The Southern Dynasties' past stirs such melancholy,
Only the Long River flows on to this day, unbound.

只有长江独自流淌至今。

title: 自夏口至鹦鹉洲夕望岳阳寄源中丞
author: 刘长卿

en_body: Upon the sandbar no waves rise, no mist drifts by,
The longing of this Chu traveler grows ever more vast.
By Hankou's setting sun birds wing obliquely across,
Dongting's autumn waters stretch to meet the sky at last.
A lone town pressed against the hills sounds cold bugle calls,
At a lonely garrison by the river my boat moors at night.
Jia Yi submitted petitions grieving for the Han house,
Exiled to Changsha, he moves all ages to pity his plight.

baihua_lines: 鹦鹉洲上没有波浪也没有烟霭，
我这楚地客子的相思之情愈发渺远。
汉口的夕阳中鸟儿斜斜飞过江面，
洞庭湖的秋水远远地与天相连。
孤城背靠着山岭传来寒天的角声，
我独自驻防临江处夜晚停泊着船。
贾谊当年上书是为汉室担忧，
被贬到长沙古往今来都令人哀怜。
baihua: [汀]洲无浪复无烟，楚客相思益渺然。汉口夕阳斜渡鸟，洞庭秋水远连天。孤城背岭寒吹角，独戍临江夜泊船。贾谊上书忧汉室，长沙谪去古今怜。
en_lines: Upon the sandbar no waves rise, no mist drifts by,
The longing of this Chu traveler grows ever more vast.
By Hankou's setting sun birds wing obliquely across,
Dongting's autumn waters stretch to meet the sky at last.
A lone town pressed against the hills sounds cold bugle calls,
At a lonely garrison by the river my boat moors at night.
Jia Yi submitted petitions grieving for the Han house,
Exiled to Changsha, he moves all ages to pity his plight.

title: 送李中丞归汉阳别业
author: 刘长卿

en_body: This general who campaigned in the south now wanders adrift,
Once he commanded a hundred thousand troops in the field.
Dismissed, he returns without any old estate to his name,
Now old, he still longs for the enlightened sovereign's weal.
Alone he stood, and the three borders grew peaceful and still,
He valued life lightly, and his sword alone knew his true worth.
Upon the vast, boundless waters of Han and Yangtze,
As the sun sets, where will you go across the earth?

en_body: For three years of exile you dwelt here in this place,
Through ten thousand ages only the sorrow of a Chu guest remains.
Alone I seek your traces amid autumn grass after you were gone,
In cold, barren woods only see the slanting sun that wanes.
Emperor Wen of Han was wise, yet his favor to you was thin,
The Xiang River knows not feeling, how could it know your lament?
In this silent land where mountains and rivers shed their leaves,
I pity you—what wrong led you to this far, distant tent?

author: 刘长卿

en_body: I watch your vessel sail into the vast misty waters,
I wave farewell, and tears wet the cloth at my wrist.
The flying bird vanishes into the distance, who knows where,
Only green mountains stand empty, facing those who part, mist-kissed.
A single sail grows distant upon the Long River,
The setting sun lights spring upon the Five Lakes.
Who can see that here upon this sandbar,
I pine for you, grieving over the white duckweed that breaks?

title: 晚次鄂州
author: 卢纶

My lone sail still has a full day's journey ahead to go.
The merchant naps by day, knowing waves are calm and still,
The boatmen chat at night, sensing the rising tide's flow.
In Sanxiang's autumn hues my temples have turned gray,
My heart yearns home ten thousand li toward the bright moon's glow.
My old homestead has perished entirely in war's ravage,
How can I bear more, hearing war drums on the river blow?

baihua: 云开远见汉阳城，犹是孤帆一日程。估客昼眠知浪静，舟人夜语觉潮生。三湘衰鬓逢秋色，万里归心对月明。旧业已随征战尽，更堪江上鼓鼙声。

My lone sail still has a full day's journey ahead to go.
The merchant naps by day, knowing waves are calm and still,
The boatmen chat at night, sensing the rising tide's flow.
In Sanxiang's autumn hues my temples have turned gray,
My heart yearns home ten thousand li toward the bright moon's glow.
My old homestead has perished entirely in war's ravage,
How can I bear more, hearing war drums on the river blow?

This time of parting fills the heart with sorrow deep and keen.
Your road leads out beyond the cold, drifting clouds,
I turn to return just as evening snow begins to fall between.

After so much hardship, I met you all too late, I ween.
We cover our faces and weep, facing each other in vain,
Amid the dust of the world, when shall we meet again, I mean?

en_body: Since we parted by rivers and seas, dear friend,
How many years have mountains and rivers kept us apart?
Meeting so suddenly, I half suspect I am dreaming,
We grieve and ask each other how old we have grown, at heart.

Over damp bamboos mist and haze silently drift and start.
Worse yet, the sorrow that tomorrow we must part again,
We cherish this farewell cup, passing it hand to heart.

Under a sky of stars you will lodge at old passes again.
Cold birds and withered grass along your journey,
Everywhere will accompany your sad face in its pain.

author: 孟浩然

note: 《夏日南亭怀辛大》是孟浩然的经典作品，语言凝练，意境深远，为历代读者所传诵。【夏日南亭怀辛大】唐代孟浩然所作的诗。
